articles.title: NCP leaders express discontent in core committee meeting after talks with Amit Shah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A day before the core committee meeting, six senior NCP leaders met Amit Shah on Sunday night and is learnt to have informed him about their unhappiness with the party’s functioning under Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar

In a core committee meeting of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) that Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar called on Monday evening (November 2, 2026), senior leaders are learnt to have expressed discontent about the style of the party’s internal functioning. The meeting lasted three hours and will be followed by a meeting of all elected legislators of the party on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

On Sunday night (November 1, 2026), six senior NCP leaders met Union Home Minister Amit Shah and are learnt to have informed him about their unhappiness with the party’s functioning under the leadership Sunetra Pawar, who is the national president of the NCP, and her son, Parth Pawar.

The leaders who met Mr. Shah are Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal, Dhananjay Munde, Hasan Mushrif, and Dilip Walse Patil, a source said. They were given an appointment to meet the BJP leader without Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar.

“There was no discussion about a merger [of the NCP with the Nationalist Congress Party–Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP)]. A merger with NCP-SP is not in the picture. What happened during the delimitation Bill debate is behind us. The meeting with Mr. Shah was specifically about the issues in the NCP. [Regarding] the way the party is being run in an authoritarian manner at present, hampering the party’s strength,” an NCP source aware of the discussion during the closed-door meeting with Mr. Shah told The Hindu on Monday (November 2, 2026).
“The Union Home Minister was already aware of the issues. The message to us was very clear. ‘Mend your ways, improve your party,’ is what was hinted to us,” top sources said.
During the NCP core committee meeting at Ms. Pawar’s residence, committee members did not mince their words while expressing their disagreements, sources told The Hindu .

Most of the six NCP leaders who met Mr. Shah are veterans with years of experience as Ministers and strong popular support. Two of them had recently called for introspection within the party after its dismal performance in the Legislative Council elections.

After the sudden demise of NCP leader and former Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar in a helicopter crash early this year, his son and political novice, Parth Pawar, had unofficially taken the reins of the party. This has caused resentment and bad blood in the party. Senior leaders have criticised his style of functioning as “authoritarian”. His political inexperience has only added to the discontent among senior leaders, who have been excluded from all key decisions in the party.

“If they (Parth Pawar and Sunetra Pawar) don’t change their way of functioning, the senior party leaders are considering charting their own way. They are not left with much of a choice, considering the unilateral decisions being taken in the party, which are completely authoritarian in nature. None of the senior leaders have been consulted for any important decision. They are unhappy about it,” a senior NCP leader told The Hindu.

Sunil Tatkare, who was one of the leaders who met Mr. Shah and is also the Maharashtra State president of the NCP, spoke to reporters after the core committee meeting and denied reports of differences within the party. However, hinting at disgruntlement, he said, “We have all worked under Sharad Pawar and later under Ajit Pawar. We have seen a particular working style and followed an organisational structure. We have believed in collective leadership, and have followed a process to take decisions. We have all worked under that system. We are now seeing how to strengthen the party under Sunetra Pawar’s leadership,” Mr. Tatkare said.

articles.title: Services of 29 contract staff at Ernakulam Government Medical College terminated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The employees, aged 60 and above, were asked to discontinue service from November. They alleged that they had been treated unfairly and their services terminated without proper notice.

The Directorate of Medical Education terminated the services of 29 contract employees of Ernakulam Government Medical College (GMC) on Sunday (November 1), leaving their families in the lurch. The employees, aged 60 and above, were asked to discontinue service from November. They alleged that they had been treated unfairly and their services terminated without proper notice.

Those whose services were terminated include nursing assistants, pharmacists and last-grade workers who had been working there since the State government took over the cooperative medical college in 2013. In 2016, the government created 315 posts to accommodate such employees. These employees had been working continuously since 2013 without a break in service. In 2026, the LDF government decided to regularise 214 contract and daily-wage employees working at the GMC, according to trade union leaders.

“Though we know that we have to discontinue service after attaining the age of 60, we should have been given proper notice. Instead, we were informed at the last moment,” said 63-year-old Salomi Baby, a native of Kothamangalam.

Harikumar A.N., a 64-year-old pharmacist whose services were also terminated, echoed her concerns. “Most people didn’t even know their services had been terminated. The order was circulated on Saturday (October 31), and everyone was asked to stop coming to work from Monday. We do not even know whether we will get the benefits due to us,” said Mr. Harikumar.

According to GMC sources, the employees had crossed the age of 60 and were ineligible to continue in service. “The decision had been communicated to them earlier as well. The staff whose services were terminated will receive pension benefits from 2016 and service seniority and benefits from 2024. They will receive these benefits when the remaining contractual employees receive the benefits after the integration process,” they said.

Meanwhile, P.M. Mujeeb Rahman, district joint secretary of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions, alleged that the move to terminate employees without recruiting enough staff could affect the GMC’s functioning. “The sudden termination without proper notice has affected the morale of the employees. It has also reduced the staff strength, severely affecting the hospital’s functioning. This even raises questions about any move to privatise the hospital,” said Mr. Rahman.

articles.title: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: While voters have reprimanded Benjamin Netanyahu for his flawed conduct, they seem to be willing to give him another chance

For the Israeli Knesset election hyped as “consequential” and a “day of reckoning for the October 7 Hamas attack”, the verdict points to new trends and the normalisation of trenchant nationalism. The inconclusive outcome risks disappointing most stakeholders. Israel, being at the epicentre of the ongoing regional tumult, needs a real-time analysis.

Israel’s total electorate is 7.3 million. Yet it has 38 officially recognised political parties vying for 120 Knesset seats, of which only 11 parties are likely to cross the 3.25% voting threshold needed to enter the legislature. The elections are on a proportional representation basis. The parties are currently arrayed in three coalitions: the ruling extreme right, the centrist bloc and the Israeli-Arab bloc which got 53, 48 and 19 seats, respectively. The last group representing a 21% minority is largely untouchable for mainstream Jewish parties. The electorate is also split along ethnic and origin-based lines into occidental, oriental and orthodox cohorts. Since the last elections in 2022, nearly half a million new voters have come of age. The voter turnout jumped by nearly a tenth to 77.7% — a sign of sharp political engagement.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: Many U.K. social care migrant workers to get PR in five years under softer immigration overhaul
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Under the scheme, finalised on November 2, social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years

Foreign social and home care workers, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, will be able to normally settle (become permanent residents) in five years, rather than in 15 years, as was first proposed in the British government’s ‘earned settlement’ scheme announced in November 2025.

Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules.

The news of softer final rules for care workers is likely to impact thousands of Indians who came in on the Health and Care Worker visa scheme, which began in October 2020 and ran until July 2025. The scheme is associated with reports of Indian care workers – including many from Kerala – being subject to abuse, including unpaid wages, illegal recruitment fees, threats and other forms of exploitation at the hands of employers.

Under the scheme, finalised on Monday (November 2, 2026), social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years. Those who have fallen afoul of the initial visa conditions would be given “a second chance”, U.K. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said, with a fresh five-year qualifying period.

“The government has already stripped around 1,800 exploitative employers of their licenses,” Ms. Mahmood said on Monday (November 2, 2026), adding that the government would help workers find positions with legitimate care providers.

The softening of the conditions for residency in the final version of the earned settlement rules, announced by Ms. Mahmood, was a response to pressure from the left flank of the Labour Party and health unions, as well as a response to a public consultation on the draft policy, conducted earlier this year. The U.K. government said that over 2,02,000 responses were received, most (73%) of whom were visa holders.

The government had originally announced the draft earned settlement scheme under pressure from the parties on the right, especially Reform U.K., which, at the time, was surging in popularity. The basis of the overhaul was to increase the default qualifying period for settlement from five to ten years, with various factors either adding to or lowering the default qualifying duration of time.

The government, headed at the time by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, had argued the immigration overhaul was necessary to counter the surge in migration (sometimes called the ‘Boriswave’) in the social care and student categories that happened after Covid, during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative.

Net migration hit a record of 9,44,000 in the year ending March 2023. However, following a tightening in policy started by the Rishi Sunak government and continued by Mr. Starmer’s Labour government, the net figure as of December 2025 dropped to 1,71,000.

“10 billion pounds. That is the cost of today’s U-turn,” shadow (i.e., opposition) Home Secretary Chris Philp said in the House of Commons on Monday (November 2, 2026), using Ms. Mahmood’s own cost estimate against her. He alleged that Ms. Mahmood was not in control of the government’s immigration policy and that Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, who is a prominent figure on Labour’s left, was in charge.

fullParagraphs: Credible studies have shown that querying an AI model with ‘anonymised’ data to extract personal details that it had memorised during training can be used to identify individuals and build their profiles

The right to privacy is a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017. However, the legal instruments currently in place to safeguard this right seem inadequate, especially considering the technological revolution led by Artificial Intelligence (AI) around the world. While AI regulation is one of the most commonly discussed issues within governments today, the recommendations have been broad, vague and have only led to further questions. AI has immense potential to boost productivity and have positive effects on people’s lives; any indiscriminate regulatory or policy measure risks inhibiting innovation and economic growth. However, there are lower hanging fruits; specific gaps that can be filled to better safeguard people’s constitutional rights without permanently losing out in the AI race.

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act was passed in 2023, with the DPDP Rules being notified in November 2025. The implementation is phased with some provisions on consent and safety becoming effective only in 2027. Prior to the DPDP Act, the primary legal instrument to regulate the use and management of personal data was the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. Together the IT Act, 2000 and its 2011 Rules broadly regulated the export of “sensitive personal data” on the condition that the recipient ensured a level of data protection required under Indian law, and that the transfer was either necessary to perform a lawful contract or had been consented to by the data provider. An assertion and claim were sufficient to record adequacy. The criminal penalty for unauthorised disclosure was capped at three years’ imprisonment or a fine of ₹5 lakh. These penalties only applied to disclosure of sensitive personal data that were listed in the Rules such as financial data, medical or health details, sexual orientation, biometric information etc. The Rules did not apply to personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, caste, religion, political affiliations, browsing history, social media activity, online or offline behavioural patterns, institutional affiliations etc.

Citing enforcement difficulties, the Bench cautioned against a blanket ban and emphasised public awareness and voluntary restraint to encourage the use of less-polluting alternatives.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: Landfall continues in Andhra Pradesh, several districts on high alert amid heavy rainfall
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several thatched houses collapsed and residents were stranded in Ongole; District Collectors informed Chief Minister Naidy that arrangements were being made for counting votes in the local body elections alongside cyclone relief operations.

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

Cyclone Murasu made its landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district, close to Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), and was expected to complete its landfall process by 6.30 a.m., Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was informed during a review with district Collectors and officials at 3.30 a.m.

The Chief Minister directed officials to ensure that people in cyclone-affected areas did not venture onto roads and to take all necessary precautions to prevent loss of life and minimise property damage. He also enquired about the condition of electricity poles and substations. Energy department officials informed him that no electricity poles had fallen and there were no disruptions to power supply anywhere. -- Sambasiva Rao

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu nears A.P. coast, heavy rain alert issued
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh government sounded an alert in five districts – Bapatla, Palnadu, Markapuram, SPSR Nellore, and Prakasam – as the severe cyclonic storm, Murasu, stayed on course to make landfall between Ongole and Nellore on the intervening night of November 2-3.
The storm is expected to bring very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to these districts, which reported a rain deficit during the monsoon.
Keep track | Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Cyclone Murasu landfall expected between Nellore and Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh tonight
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the storm is likely to move with a “wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph (and) gusting up to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narasapur”.
In the wake of Marasu, heavy rain fell in the northern districts of Tamil Nadu bordering Andhra Pradesh from Sunday evening, and some parts of north Chennai reported waterlogging.
In Odisha, where rain triggered by Cyclone Arnab caused widespread damage last week, the government evacuated 1.6 lakh people across Ganjam, Gajapati, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Kandhamal districts.

The IMD said the storm was located about 80 km east-northeast of Nellore, 80 km east-southeast of Kavali, 110 km southeast of Ongole, 140 km south of Bapatla, 170 km south-southwest of Machilipatnam, 170 km northeast of Tirupati, and 190 km north-northeast of Nungambakkam in Chennai.

The system is moving towards the coast at 12 kmph, and gales of 70-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, have been reported along the Andhra Pradesh coast. A storm surge is expected in coastal areas to the north of the landfall point, the IMD said.
IMD, Amaravati, issued a red alert for Palnadu, Tirupati, and Nandyal districts on Tuesday, and an orange alert is in place for 12 districts.

In Chennai, as the cyclone’s outer bands brushed Tamil Nadu’s northern coast, the Regional Meteorological Centre upgraded weather alerts for northern districts such as Chennai and Tiruvallur on Monday (November 2, 2026). It warned of squally winds, gusting up to 75 kmph, in various northern districts, including Chennai and Kancheepuram till Tuesday (November 3) morning.

As the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ over the Bay of Bengal began to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Kothapatnam, around 20 km from Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), it brought very heavy rainfall to the two districts of Prakasam and Bapatla overnight.
In one night, the overall rainfall deficit of Prakasam district, which stood at a little over 64% as of November 2, came down to 58.6%.

Between 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026) and 12 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), there was a lull in the rainfall activity in districts that were likely to be affected by the cyclone. However, as the storm began moving closer to the land, many weather stations in Central A.P. and South Coastal A.P. received received very heavy rainfall of around 200 mm within six hours.

According to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), which provides realtime weather information in all 688 mandals of the State, as of 6 a.m., Naguluppalapadu recorded the maximum of 198.01 mm rainfall, followed by Kothapatnam at 182.25 mm, Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University area in Bapatla district recorded 128.53 mm, Chirala recorded 124.1 mm, Bapatla town recorded 119.75 mm.

Narsapuram of West Godavari district, where the Very Severe Cyclonic Storm made the landfall, recorded 109 mm rainfall. Ongole Urban recorded 106 mm rainfall and Chilakapadu of Prakasam district recorded 104.5 mm rainfall. West Godavari and Krishna districts also recorded moderate showers during the night.

Meanwhile, the landfall process is likely to continue till 9 a.m. The storm may move north-northwestwards and weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm by noon and further into a deep depression by Tuesday midnight. But, the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority(APSDMA) has alerted the public as gale winds may continue in Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts till noon.
According to reports, vehicles have been stopped in the early morning hours on a highway near Ongole, due to gales of speed reaching 90-100 kmph. (There are two highways, not sure which yet).

A storm surge warning has also been given, as a surge of 1.0-1.5 metres height above astronomical tide is expected to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal line in the districts of Bapatla and Krishna.

articles.title: Activists raise concern over Supreme Court order on green firecrackers, traders lament stock availability
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital

The Supreme Court’s decision on Monday (November 2, 2026) to allow green firecrackers on November 7 and 8 has raised concerns over its implementation, with environmental activists questioning how the restrictions can be enforced at such short notice and traders warning that the limited window leaves them little time to procure stocks.
Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital.

In 2019, when only green crackers were allowed and several months were given to prepare for implementing it, Delhi still saw the decision being openly flouted and also there was a lack of stock in many shops.
Later, the Delhi government moved to a complete ban, including green firecrackers, for a few months around Diwali, but that too was flouted on a large scale.

Last year, the Supreme Court passed a order similar to this year, lifting the ban temporarily to allow green firecrackers to be burst for a fixed window of time for two days during Deepavali. But this ban was also openly flouted and the air turned toxic with many air quality monitoring stations in Delhi being unable to record the level of air pollution as they maxed out.

“Unless there is a blanket ban on firecrackers, people will burst all types of firecrackers in the city. We have seen that over the years, including last year. Even after the ban was reimposed after Deepavali last year, people continued to burst firecrackers for marriages, concerts and everything else in Delhi,” said Bhavreen Kandhari, an environmental activist.

“There are no green firecrackers available in the market. Also, who will check on the ground, and how, what type of firecrackers people are bursting? The air will be toxic again after Deepavali,” she added.
ALSO WATCH Watch: SC limits Delhi-NCR Deepavali fireworks to three hours across designated time slots on November 7, 8

Rajiv Kumar Jain, 68, a member of the Delhi Fireworks Traders Association, said traders welcomed the court order but were concerned that the short notice would leave them with little time to procure sufficient stocks of green firecrackers.

“Our permanent licences have been suspended, and we need to get them reinstated tomorrow. We can sell only on November 4, 5 and 6. That leaves us only one day to get the firecrackers from the manufacturers, which is very difficult,” Mr. Jain said.

articles.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Along with their results, Petronet LNG also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share

State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.

articles.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are non-citizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections.
The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls.
It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term.

In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.

The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump's push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.
The Republican Trump administration has prioritized identifying noncitizen voters this year, despite them being rare.
A district court judge previously denied the Justice Department's request and warned that the demand could disenfranchise citizens in Tuesday's midterm elections to determine control of Congress.

Also on Monday (November 2, 2026) in Washington, another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution. “The Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution's Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone,” wrote Chief Judge James Boasberg.
The administration, for its part, said segregating the ballots was a modest request that would eventually allow legal votes to still be counted.

The administration has faced a remarkable string of losses in court in its push, as well as criticism for waiting until a few weeks before the election to make its demands of California election officials with a list that even the Department of Justice admits is not entirely reliable.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are non-citizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections.

The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls.

It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term.

In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.

The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump's push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.

The Republican Trump administration has prioritized identifying noncitizen voters this year, despite them being rare.

A district court judge previously denied the Justice Department's request and warned that the demand could disenfranchise citizens in Tuesday's midterm elections to determine control of Congress.

Also on Monday (November 2, 2026) in Washington, another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution. “The Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution's Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone,” wrote Chief Judge James Boasberg.

The administration, for its part, said segregating the ballots was a modest request that would eventually allow legal votes to still be counted.

The administration has faced a remarkable string of losses in court in its push, as well as criticism for waiting until a few weeks before the election to make its demands of California election officials with a list that even the Department of Justice admits is not entirely reliable.

articles.title: Venezuela's Opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile, as doubts over democracy deepen
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Acting President Delcy Rodriguez was initially supposed to serve only 90 days as acting president, but has remained in office and has made no move to call an election

Opposition leader and Nobel laureate Maria Corina Machado reappeared in Venezuela on Sunday (October 25, 2026) for the first time since December, returning from exile at a time when doubts about the country's democratic future — and the role of the U.S. —are growing.

It was her first appearance since the U.S. military deposed the country's then-President Nicolás Maduro, replacing him with an interim president who has exceeded the time she was authorised to serve, with no election scheduled.
Ms. Machado announced her arrival on social media, writing, “I am here. With you.”
Another leading figure in the Venezuelan opposition, Edmundo González, wrote on X confirming that Ms. Machado had arrived and that he would be next to her “very soon.”
“Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” he wrote. “You know it, this is until the end.”

On Sunday afternoon (October 25, 2026), Ms. Machado strode into a church in the town of Lara, west of Caracas, to the applause of dozens gathered there as they shook her hand and hugged her, with cell phones aloft to record her return. “Maria! Maria!” someone cried out.

Asked by reporters on Sunday (October 25, 2026) about Ms. Machado's return to Venezuela, U.S. President Donald Trump said, “I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing really well in Venezuela.”
Since Mr. Maduro's ouster, Venezuela has been run by acting President Delcy Rodriguez, a longtime Maduro ally who received the Trump administration's blessing to succeed him.
Ms. Rodriguez was initially supposed to serve only 90 days as acting president, but has remained in office and has made no move to call an election.

Ms. Machado was briefly detained in January 2025, following a protest against Mr. Maduro's planned swearing-in ceremony, and went into hiding in Venezuela for 11 months. After making a clandestine escape from the country, she reappeared that December in Norway, where she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her peaceful challenge to Mr. Maduro's authoritarian government.

articles.title: Netanyahu pressing Trump to attack Iran after midterms, says officials
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Benjamin Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Mr. Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. U.S. President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran's ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American, and in one case Israeli, officials.

One official said Mr. Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the U.S. administration to persuade Mr. Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.
Mr. Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Mr. Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other U.S. allies in West Asia are warning against more strikes, saying it would destabilise the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.
That official, and the person familiar with the Netanyahu-Trump call, were not authorised to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Israeli government did not immediately comment. The White House did not directly respond to questions about Mr. Netanyahu and Mr. Trump's discussion of potential new strikes during the weekend call.

Mr. Trump told reporters on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that he and Mr. Netanyahu had a “very good” call the day before. He said they discussed Iran but gave no details. Mr. Netanyahu had pushed for renewed strikes even before the Israeli election as he sought to highlight his security credentials to a public deeply scarred by Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack.

articles.title: Bihar Assembly serves notice to Anant Singh over plea to expel him
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mokama MLA has been given a week’s time to respond to the charges against him

The Bihar Assembly served notice on Mokama MLA Anant Singh on Monday (November 2, 2026), asking him to respond within a week to the plea by the Janata Dal (United) seeking the revocation of his Assembly membership.

On October 24, following the results of elections to eight State Legislative Council seats, in which Mr. Singh had opposed party’s official candidate Neeraj Kumar, the JD(U) expelled the Mokama MLA and his wife, Neelam Devi, for “anti-party activities” for six years. Mr. Kumar went on to win the seat.

Ms. Devi was also removed from the membership of the government’s 20-point programme committee, which had given her the status of a Deputy Minister. She was also asked to vacate the official bungalow in Patna. Two days after the election results, the ruling National Democratic Alliance partner had requested the Speaker to rescind the Mokama lawmaker’s Assembly membership.

On the directive of the State assembly Speaker Prem Kumar, the secretary of the House served notice Mr. Singh asking him to respond the charges made against him within a week’s time by November 9. A series of charges including several newspaper reports and a video CD was also submitted by the JD(U) leaders to the Assembly Speaker’s office on October 26 to rescind his membership from the House, party sources had earlier told The Hindu.

State JD(U) President Umesh Kushwaha and party MLC Sanjay Kumar Singh alias Gandhi, who is considered close to party chief Nitish Kumar, had gone to the office of State assembly Speaker on October 26 with charges against the Mokarna MLA and requested for a “quick action” against him. “The Speaker was not in the office at that time “but, we’re assured for a quick action”, Mr. Kushwaha later told media persons.
On October 30, the Supreme Court directed the expelled MLA to surrender by December 1 in connection with murder of Dular Chand Yadav, for which he was arrested last year.
Mr. Singh said he would comply with the apex court’s order.

articles.title: Police foil bid to snatch smuggled gold from woman at Karipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her

The police foiled an attempt to abduct a woman carrying 817 gm gold worth over ₹1.10 crore at Calicut International Airport, Karipur, on Monday. They also arrested two members of the alleged robbery gang.

According to the police, the incident took place around 3 a.m. A police team noticed a group behaving suspiciously in the arrival area and kept them under watch. The group followed Abhirami, 27, a native of Vandanmedu in Idukki, after she arrived from abroad.

When Abhirami reached the parking area with a man who had come to receive her, the gang blocked their way and grabbed her trolley bag. The police team intervened when the gang tried to overpower the man accompanying her.

During the struggle, the accused attacked the police and bit home guard Murali Krishna. They also tried to run over a member of the police team with a car while escaping. The officer narrowly escaped from being hit.
The police arrested Sayanth, 28, and Babilesh, 40, both from Kallachi, Nadapuram.
Abhirami and Harshal, 40, a native of Kochi who had arrived to collect the gold, were also taken into custody.
The police said the gold had been sent with Abhirami by Swalih, a native of Thamarassery. Around 10 people had reached the airport in two cars to seize the gold and abduct her.
A search of Abhirami’s baggage led to the recovery of 14 gold plates concealed inside an emergency lamp. The gold weighed 817 gm after cleaning and is estimated to be worth more than ₹1.10 crore.

The gold, along with ₹67,000 allegedly kept to pay Abhirami for carrying it, a car and the two people detained in connection with the gold, were handed over to the Customs Department for further action.
The police said the arrested men had been involved in several similar cases. One of them had lost a hand in a blast.

articles.title: U.S. votes for midterm elections, seen as referendum on Trump
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The polling will decide whether President Trump’s Republican Party retains control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of the U.S. Congress, or, as opinion polls are predicting, the Democratic Party wrests control of at least the House if not the Senate, also in the final two years of Mr. Trump’s second term in office

Americans will vote on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) in one of the most consequential elections in recent times , widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s presidency that has been marked by a prolonged war in Iran , rising inflation, trade wars and deep divisions in society.

The polling will decide whether President Trump’s Republican Party retains control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of the U.S. Congress, or, as opinion polls are predicting, the Democratic Party wrests control of at least the House if not the Senate, also in the final two years of Mr. Trump’s second term in office.
At stake in the elections are all 435 seats of the House and 37 seats in the 100-member Senate.

Elections are also being held for the post of Governor in 36 states, including in Ohio, where Indian American Vivek Ramaswamy is locked in a keen contest with his rival and Democratic nominee Amy Acton.

Several Indian American candidates are in the electoral fray for posts ranging from Governor to city council member. Democrat Nithya Raman, born in Kerala, is locked in a tight contest with her former boss, Karen Bass, for the mayor's seat in Los Angeles, the second-largest city in the U.S..

Indian-American lawmakers Ro Khanna, Ami Bera, Pramila Jayapal and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. House of Representatives, while fellow Democrats Pia Dandiya and Amish Shah are in the fray in competitive races to make their debut as Congresspersons.

On Monday (November 2), the Republicans and the Democrats made their final pitch to the voters, with Mr. Trump choosing an unusual venue — the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — to focus on the renovations undertaken in the national capital instead of talking about tax cuts, tariffs and border security, which have been the high points of his election rallies.

According to the White House, Mr. Trump did a whirlwind tour of 20 states, mostly Republican strongholds, to address 30 rallies in the last 32 days. Analysts say his approval ratings are at an all-time low, and he has become a liability to Republican candidates.

If the pre-poll forecasts come true and Democrats take control of the U.S. Congress, it will allow for deeper Congressional scrutiny and checks on Mr. Trump’s actions, which will severely limit his ability to push his agenda. He will, however, retain the power to govern through executive orders, which will be valid for two years.
Mr. Trump acknowledged the possibility of his wings being clipped but indicated that he would not allow Congress to slow him down.

fullParagraphs: Vice-President J.D. Vance told reporters that he just spoke to President Trump about talks with Iran and said that “the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement”
The U.S. has conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, a U.S. official says.

Iranian state television reported that explosions were heard on Qeshm Island. The official, who wasn't authorised to comment publicly and spoke on Monday (November 2, 2026) on condition of anonymity, said “Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets” had been targeted.

The strikes, which appeared to be limited as opposed to a full return to hostilities, came on the eve of crucial American midterm elections. Mr. Trump has previously said the U.S. wouldn't launch strikes on Iran before the midterms.
The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on U.S. gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

Vice-President J.D. Vance told reporters that he just spoke to Mr. Trump about talks with Iran and said that “the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement.”

Mr. Vance offered measured optimism on Monday (November 2, 2026) that a deal can still be struck to prevent President Donald Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the crucial midterm elections in the United States.

Mr. Vance sent a letter to Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, last week, but the White House has offered scant details about the contents of that correspondence. Mr. Trump told reporters that letter was focused on assisting Iran with “medical supplies and various things.” But he suggested there's reason to believe that the U.S. and Iran could still come to an agreement.

“We've had a number of good conversations with the Iranians,” Mr. Vance told reporters when asked about the letter. “I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this. Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We're going to keep on working at it.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Mr. Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal with Iran.

articles.title: Israel’s far-right supporters hold out hope for return to power
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: After years of the Israeli electorate drifting rightwards under Mr. Netanyahu, far-right parties such as Mr. Ben Gvir’s Jewish Power and Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism had hoped for watershed gains
Itamar Ben Gvir, the far-right Israeli firebrand who achieved international notoriety as part of the outgoing government, fell short of expectations that he would gain ground in the latest election.
But support remains. Under the blazing sun of Sderot, a southern city not far from the Gaza border, bakery employee Yaakov Peretz said he believed Mr. Ben Gvir would remain a central force.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu “needs Ben Gvir by his side, strong and stable, with right-wing views”, Mr. Peretz told AFP as he took a smoke break.

After years of the Israeli electorate drifting rightwards under Mr. Netanyahu, far-right parties such as Mr. Ben Gvir’s Jewish Power and Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism had hoped for watershed gains in last week’s vote.

But by the time the dust had settled, they had netted the same number of seats they had before — 13 between them — not enough to crown them an ascendant force, but enough to cement their place in the political landscape.

Long seen as an unpalatable troublemaker among the more mainstream right, and convicted as a younger man on charges including incitement to racism, Ben Gvir ascended to national Security Minister in Mr. Netanyahu’s government.
With Finance Minister Smotrich, he embodied the most radical wing of the outgoing coalition.

Mr. Ben Gvir has called for “voluntary” emigration of Palestinians from Gaza and the West Bank, routine killings of “30 or 40” people in Gaza per night, and for cutting food and sanitation for Palestinian prisoners to the bare minimum.
Relishing his power, before the election he openly said he wanted to be Defence Minister.

But after enjoying unprecedented influence for the last four years, the far right is increasingly likely to find itself back on the sidelines, watching as more mainstream parties haggle to form a new governing coalition.

articles.title: Kerala HC allows plea by Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit against permitting suspended students to appear for examinations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna held that the single Bench erred in issuing the directions in the absence of evidence from the students demonstrating their eligibility to appear for the examinations

The Kerala High Court has allowed a petition filed by Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady against permitting 16 suspended students to appear for the semester examinations set to begin on November 4, 2026. Ciza Thomas, Vice-Chancellor, along with the varsity Syndicate had moved the Kerala High Court seeking to set aside a single Bench order which allowed the suspended students of the university to write the semester examinations.

They had challenged the single Bench order to accept the examination fee from the students and provisionally permit them to write the examinations. The Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna held that the single Bench erred in issuing the directions in the absence of evidence from the students demonstrating their eligibility to appear for the examinations, including the required internal assessment marks and attendance.

The court noted that the students had sought to appear for the examinations without filing an application to condone shortage of attendance. It also held that no court was authorised to direct a university to act in contravention of the regulations governing the academic course. The court also noted that the single Bench had not granted the university an opportunity to respond to the students’ plea while issuing the directions.
The students were under suspension pending inquiry for allegedly staging a mock funeral of the vice-chancellor and attempting to damage her property.

articles.title: Supreme Court grants liberty to Abhishek Banerjee, asks Calcutta HC to consider plea against media trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said that Abhishek Banerjee can mention for hearing the matter on the reopening of the High Court

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) granted relief to Lok Sabha MP Abhishek Banerjee and asked the Calcutta High Court to consider his plea against media trial related to investigations and cases against him.
A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said that Mr. Banerjee can mention for hearing the matter on the reopening of the High Court.
Senior advocate Shoeb Alam, appearing for Mr. Banerjee, said that the matter was taken up for hearing only once by the HC, when the petitioner was told that it did not have the roster.
"Since then, I have mentioned the matter three times before the High Court but the petition has not been taken up for hearing but there is continuing violation of my rights," Mr. Alam submitted.
He contended that this Court has in several judgments held that the presumption of innocence cannot be taken away by media trials.

The Bench noted that the HC was reopening on November 16 after Durga Puja and Diwali break, and the petitioner was at liberty to mention the matter for consideration of the interim relief. It asked the Court to consider Mr. Banerjee's plea.

The Lok Sabha MP has sought an order in the HC restraining investigating agencies from sharing his personal information with media outlets and alleged that selective leaks by the investigating officer (IO) were tarnishing his image. He said these could also influence the ongoing investigations against him.

Mr. Banerjee, who is under investigation in multiple cases, has alleged that probe agencies were leaking details of searches, interrogations and other legal steps to a section of the media and several news articles have appeared in different newspapers.

He has contended that such deliberate leaks by police officials violated his rights to dignity, reputation and a fair investigation under Article 21 of the Constitution, and could tarnish his public image while influencing the investigations against him.
Mr. Banerjee has sought direction restraining media outlets from reporting or publishing news about him relating to matters forming part of the ongoing investigations.

fullParagraphs: The Telangana State Commission for Women has sought detailed reports from the Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Medchal Malkajgiri Police Commissioners on illegal human egg collection racket and exploitation of economically vulnerable women by organised gangs in Saroornagar and Begumpet.

In a letter dated November 1, the Commission directed the three police Commissioners to submit a comprehensive action-taken report by Tuesday (November 3, 2026), taking note of media reports about the arrest of gangs allegedly involved in collecting human eggs from women in the two areas.

The Commission expressed concern over reports that organised gangs allegedly recruited women from Telangana and other States by offering monetary incentives, exploiting their financial difficulties and transporting them to undisclosed locations. The women were administered hormonal injections and subjected to medical procedures for collection of human eggs, potentially putting their physical and reproductive health at risk.
It also flagged concerns over the possible trafficking and illegal confinement of women, besides violations of their rights, dignity and safety.

The Commission has asked the police to furnish details of the incidents, cases registered and action taken against the accused, agents and other persons allegedly involved in the racket. It has also sought information on the number of women rescued and their present whereabouts, including details of shelter, medical assistance, counselling, protection and rehabilitation provided to them.

Further, the police have been asked to provide details of investigations into the possible involvement of hospitals, fertility centres, medical practitioners and other persons, and steps taken to identify other women who may have been affected.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu’s economic performance cannot be assessed merely by gross GST revenue: Commercial Taxes Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu’s actual GST revenue had registered 15% growth up to October in the current financial year, while recording 8% growth in October alone, said Logesh Tamilselvan.

Amid criticism from Opposition parties that the State’s growth rate in Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue had fallen below the national average under the TVK government, Minister for Commercial Taxes and Registration D. Logesh Tamilselvan said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) it was incorrect to assess Tamil Nadu’s economic performance solely on the basis of gross GST collection figures.

In a post on X, the Minister said it was important to understand how GST figures were calculated. Gross GST collection includes SGST, the Union government’s CGST and IGST. However, the entire IGST collected cannot be considered revenue belonging to Tamil Nadu, as it also includes amounts attributable to other States.
Citing GST revenue decline, Stalin says Tamil Nadu is ‘doomed’ under TVK government
Palaniswami expresses concern over lower growth rate in Tamil Nadu’s GST collections
T.N.’s GST collection over past six months raises serious questions about its economy: Annamalai

He said Tamil Nadu’s actual GST revenue comprises SGST collections and the IGST settlement apportioned to the State. Following the GST rate rationalisation in September 2025, tax rates on several commodities were reduced. Therefore, the State’s economic performance could not be assessed merely on the basis of a decline in gross GST collections, he argued.
He said Tamil Nadu’s actual GST revenue had registered 15% growth up to October in the current financial year, while recording 8% growth in October alone.
Tamil Nadu / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / taxes and duties

articles.title: ‘Absolute disgrace’: Congress slams Modi govt bid to reclaim IAF Sports Complex
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Air Force Sports Complex's management was issued eviction notices by the government, demanding the return of the land situated near the Prime Minister's official residence

The Congress on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) attacked the Centre over its bid to reclaim the land on which the Indian Air Force Sports Complex is built, saying the Modi government's actions are an "absolute disgrace" and show "utter disrespect" to the entire IAF family.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared on X a media report which claimed that on October 26, days before his October 31 retirement, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh urged Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to protect the Indian Air Force (IAF)'s control of the prime land within the Race Course Air Force Station, near the Prime Minister's residence, citing operational imperatives and the facilities located there.

In his post, Mr. Ramesh said, "The IAF Sports Complex has a long history and has, over the decades, served many public purposes, as well as being an integral part of the Indian Air Force social infrastructure."
"The Modi government's actions are an absolute disgrace and show utter disrespect to the entire IAF family," Mr. Ramesh added.
The Race Course Air Force Station's sports complex — which featured a golf course, a swimming pool, and other amenities — was closed last Wednesday.

The Land and Development Office (L&DO), operating under the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, issued eviction notices to the complex's management, demanding the return of the land situated near the Prime Minister's official residence at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg.
This move comes as part of the Centre's recent drive to reclaim high-value land parcels across the area.

Over the past several weeks, the government has initiated a review of prime land parcels near Lok Kalyan Marg through the L&DO with a view to reclaiming plots used for defence golf and sports facilities.
The Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry had earlier asked the entities concerned to hand over the land housing the Air Force Golf Course.
In August, the department evicted the Delhi Race Club from its 53-acre premises on Lok Kalyan Marg, citing the requirement of the land for an unspecified public purpose.

articles.title: Demonstrations generate ‘protest economy’, Supreme Court tells Delhi traders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bench expressed sympathy for the right to livelihood of the small traders, hawkers and push cart vendors, noting that their right competed with the right to expression of the protestors

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) remarked to Delhi traders that protests are not entirely hostile to business, pointing out that there is also “protest economy” that generates brisk earnings for enterprising hawkers and vendors at demonstration sites.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed sympathy for the right to livelihood of the small traders, hawkers, push cart vendors, noting that their right competed with the right to expression of the protestors. The court said there was a need for balance.

“Right to protest is constitutionally recognised. Right to trade is also. By ‘trade’ we do not mean commercial establishments, but those who do it as the sole source of livelihood, like the daily wagers, the subjiwala, etc. Where can they go?” Chief Justice Kant observed.

The court was responding to a petition filed by Kirana Committee Delhi that protests are “bleeding” the traders of Delhi dry during the two months of peak festive season around Dussehra and Deepavali.

Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for the national capital’s traders, said even the Ramlila Grounds, the designated protest site after Jantar Mantar, was only a mile away from the iconic shopping and commercial hub of Connaught Place (CP) in the national capital.

Mr. Rohatgi even detailed the one-mile route from CP and through Minto Road to Ramlila Grounds, saying the latter was not as far as everyone thought from the business centre in the heart of the capital city.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench, said the court would take Mr. Rohatgi’s word for it as he was “the son of the soil of Delhi”.

“We have lost thousands of crores. Nobody is able to do business in Connaught Place. Thousands of auxiliary workers connected to these businesses are without a jobs as sales is down in the middle of the festive season,” Mr. Rohatgi said.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the Union government, referred to how the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-linked NEET-UG paper leak protestors had sought permission for a peaceful demonstration at Jantar Mantar only for a day on June 20, but had refused to leave. The demonstration had ultimately culminated in violence after the protestors took out a ‘Sansad Chalo’ march to the Parliament on July 20 without taking any permission from the authorities.

“Everybody has a right to protest… But everybody must adhere to conditions of permission. You cannot occupy a protest site indefinitely. There are other protestors too… Where will they go?” Chief Justice Kant asked.

articles.title: Iran unveils huge billboard with threat against Donald Trump’s life
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: We will kill Trump, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran

Iran unveiled a massive billboard and banners pledging to kill U.S. President Donald Trump across Tehran on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), bringing to a new level the official rhetoric displayed in the capital.
“We will kill Trump”, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran, which depicted the U.S. president behind bars with his head bowed.

Another billboard nearby showed Trump along with U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance , special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with bloodied faces and ragged suits against the background of worn-out Israeli and U.S. flags.

Dozens of people gathered in the square waving red flags and carrying banners reading: “There will be blood” while calling for revenge for slain supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in U.S.-Israeli attacks on February 28, triggering the Middle East war.
New designs of billboards and displays mocking and vowing revenge against Mr. Trump and boasting of victory over the United States in the war have frequently been set up around Tehran.

In recent days, renewed diplomatic efforts have been underway to bring Tehran and Washington to negotiate to prevent a resumption in fighting which has spread across the region and driven prices up globally.
Mr. Trump, who on Tuesday (November 3) faces crucial U.S. midterm elections amid voter discontent driven in part by the Iran war, has said that a deal “could happen”.

articles.title: California could become first U.S. State to tax billionaires' wealth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare

California could become the first State in the United States to tax the net worth of billionaires , it was proposed on Tuesday (November 3. 2026) under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in the State’s history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee.
Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders has framed the proposal as a monumental step toward reining in deep wealth inequality by ensuring the ultra-rich pay their fair share. But Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom warns it would prompt the State's wealthiest to move out of California and take their tax money with them.

The “no” side has raised roughly 10 times as much as the “yes” side, thanks in large part to tech moguls and venture capitalists, who have poured millions into a political action committee fighting the measure. Billionaires are already bracing for its approval. Some of them, including Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, started cutting ties with the State after the measure was unveiled. Mark Zuckerberg said he would stay in California for eight years and made a deal with Meta that would help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.

Backers of the proposed tax, led by the powerful labor union SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, say it's needed to help the State backfill the federal funding cuts. The union estimates the state will lose $100 billion in federal healthcare funding over five years.
“It's time to collect those taxes so we can ensure that our healthcare system is still safe,” said Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions.

But some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Teachers Association, are part of a coalition opposing it. They're concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the State's budget if there's a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers. California's budget relies heavily on the income tax of the State's richest residents.

Likely voters were slightly more likely to oppose the measure than support it in a poll conducted in mid-October by the Public Policy Institute of California, with 52% saying they would vote “no” and 46% saying they would vote “yes.” That's an apparent shift from a PPIC survey conducted in early September, when 52% of likely voters said they'd vote for the tax and 46% said they'd vote against it.
Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who's politically independent, said he planned to vote against it.
“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don't believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don't believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”

fullParagraphs: The largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world was hit by an approximately $6.3 billion hack, the biggest in history, yet customers got their crypto back in about 3-4 days

The story so far: Early morning on October 29, many customers at Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, began receiving messages that their accounts were being unexpectedly emptied. What followed, over the course of just about 20 minutes, was the biggest crypto hack in history, with more than $6 billion worth being stolen. By November 2, Binance had replaced 100% of the stolen amount to customers. The search for the culprit and recovery process still continues, but the customer impact has been mitigated in a remarkably short time.

Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. According to Binance, a preliminary investigation points to a “compromised” laptop belonging to one of its engineers that could have allowed the hacker to submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.

articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York's first such death in 30 years
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease
A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the State's first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The child died in Lewis County, about 93 miles (150 kilometres) north of Syracuse, Governor Kathy Hochul said.

The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

Ms. Hochul, a Democrat, said the child's death is “a devastating reminder of what's at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.”

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed three measles-associated deaths in the U.S. this year, but State health departments have reported higher numbers. Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths this year and are investigating a possible sixth.

Ms. Hochul declared a disaster emergency in early October because of measles cases in neighbouring States and in rural areas of New York. The executive order extended the pool of people who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, midwives and others, and it allowed nurses to join doctors in ordering testing.

The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease

A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the State's first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced on Monday (November 2, 2026).

The child died in Lewis County, about 93 miles (150 kilometres) north of Syracuse, Governor Kathy Hochul said.

The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

Ms. Hochul, a Democrat, said the child's death is “a devastating reminder of what's at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.”

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed three measles-associated deaths in the U.S. this year, but State health departments have reported higher numbers. Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths this year and are investigating a possible sixth.

Ms. Hochul declared a disaster emergency in early October because of measles cases in neighbouring States and in rural areas of New York. The executive order extended the pool of people who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, midwives and others, and it allowed nurses to join doctors in ordering testing.

articles.title: WHO urged to review drinking water standards amid nitrate health fears
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Surface water models indicate that hundreds of millions of people globally are exposed to elevated nitrate levels, the letter warned

Dozens of global health and environmental organisations called on the World Health Organization on Tuesday to revise decades-old standards for nitrate levels in drinking water, arguing they do not reflect recent scientific evidence about potential health risks.

In an open letter, 85 organisations, including Greenpeace International and the World Organization of Family Doctors (WONCA), called on the United Nations health agency to include nitrate in an upcoming review of its drinking water guidelines.
The toxic effects of nitrates -- a residue left behind by intensive farming -- are widely recognised as particularly dangerous for children and pregnant women.

But the current WHO guidelines -- which set the maximum acceptable nitrate level in drinking water at 50 milligrammes per litre as nitrate or 11.3 milligrammes per litre as nitrate-nitrogen -- date back to 1958 and are "outdated", the organisations warned.
That level was set specifically to prevent so-called "blue-baby syndrome" -- a deadly blood disorder in which the blood's capacity for carrying oxygen is reduced.

But the limit "has not been updated in response to robust epidemiological evidence linking chronic, low-level nitrate exposure to long-term human health risks", Tuesday's letter said, pointing in particular to "colorectal cancer and adverse birth outcomes".
"Studies now link nitrate in drinking water, at levels well below the current WHO limit, to bowel cancer and premature birth," WONCA chair Pratyush Kumar said in a joint statement.
The letter was sent to coincide with WHO's annual One Health Day, which aims to raise awareness about the interconnected health of humans, animals, plants and shared ecosystems.
Surface water models indicate that hundreds of millions of people globally are exposed to elevated nitrate levels, the letter warned.
"Water should be life-giving, not life-threatening," Amanda Larsson, the global project lead for agriculture at Greenpeace, said in the statement.

articles.title: HP launches OmniBook 5 and ProBook 4 G2iS in India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The AI-ready laptops are targeted at students and mobile professionals in India

HP on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) launched the OmniBook 5 and HP ProBook 4 G2iS laptops in India . Designed for flexible learning and hybrid working, the AI-ready devices feature Intel Core 7 processors, integrated NPU capabilities, and OLED displays.

The student-focused HP OmniBook 5 features an 11.77mm aluminum chassis weighing 1.16kg. Powered by up to an Intel Core 7 processor with a 16 TOPS NPU, it offers a cinematic OLED display with a 90 percent screen-to-body ratio and up to 42 hours of local video playback battery life.

Aimed at business professionals, the HP ProBook 4 G2iS features a 12mm thin profile weighing 1.18kg. It packs up to an Intel Core 7 processor with a 17 TOPS NPU, 32GB RAM, and 1TB storage. It sports a 14-inch 2.8K OLED screen, 70Whr battery, AI Noise Reduction, and HP Drive Lock.

The HP OmniBook 5 14 is open for pre-booking until November 10 on the HP Online and HP World Stores starting at ₹1,09,999. It comes in Smoke Silver, Starlit Blue, Peony Pink, and Soft Honeydew options. Meanwhile, the HP ProBook 4 G2iS 14 starts at ₹86,000 plus taxes, available starting November 6.
