articles.title: What India’s leaky exam system can learn from Soviet shoe factories
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Unless we treat the exams as the complex economic product they are, with knowledge dispersed among specialised professionals and each player acting in their own self-interest, and restructure the financial incentives at play, we will keep having protests and Cabinet reshuffles and Committee appointments

While the protests in New Delhi, the Centre relenting, and the petitions at the Supreme Court bent the arc of justice towards the lakhs of students who had suffered from leaked examination papers, neither the Cockroach Janta Party-led opposition nor the ruling dispensation have offered any concrete steps to prevent future leaks, beyond administrative reshuffles and legislative amendments. Neither seems wiser than the other.

The operations of the National Testing Agency (NTA) bear an uncanny resemblance to those of state-owned shoe factories in Soviet Russia. Since these factories were not driven by consumer demand, factories could meet the required production quotas they got from above by producing N number of pairs within a narrow range of sizes, regardless of whether they lay unsold on the shelves. Sure, shoe prices had been kept frozen for decades, calculated as a percentage of the lowest government wage, but the shoes did not fit your feet. Workers and lower management had no incentives to be resource-efficient, and pilferage of leather, glue, and rubber was rampant.

articles.title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus to face first earnings test as memory costs surge
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent

John Ternus will host his first earnings call as ‌Apple’s CEO on Monday, with investors looking to the company’s forecast to determine whether ​a blitz of new products can help offset rising costs for memory chips.

Ternus, ⁠who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple’s first foldable phone, smart home hub and Apple’s first touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company’s current fiscal first quarter, amid ‌what Cook had called a “100-year flood” of rising memory costs.

Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, Ternus’ remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and ‌rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six ‌quarters.
Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent, which took App Store rankings by storm in recent weeks.

Rivals such as OpenAI, which Apple is suing over alleged trade-secret theft, are also developing devices aimed at displacing the iPhone as the central device in people’s lives. How Apple ​embraces AI could also have large implications ‌for the future of its services business, whose slowing growth has worried investors after years of rapid expansion.

“Recent agentic innovation far outpaces our experience with Siri AI, but Apple has acknowledged that Siri AI ... is far more focused on trust/privacy,” said Dan Morgan, portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, which owns ‌Apple shares.
Apple is marketing Apple’s AI systems toward “everyday people” rather than Silicon Valley insiders, who ​are big users of frontier AI models from the likes of OpenAI.
Morgan added that investors want to know whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through ⁠its App Store and taking a cut of the business they generate.

For now, Apple’s reluctance to join the massive AI spending race has worked in its favour. Its shares have risen about 27% this year, ‌outperforming tech giants such as Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon as investors seek shelter from mounting concerns over the cost of building AI infrastructure.

Analysts expect Apple to report a nearly 11% rise in revenue to $113.39 billion for the July-September period, the company’s fiscal fourth quarter, according to LSEG data. Net profit is expected to rise about 6% to $29.04 billion.

fullParagraphs: Agri-food thinktank Vrihi Foundation’s new report explores how indigenous agricultural and forest produce such as turmeric, jamun, and mahua can gain stronger value chains, markets and policy support

Over the last few years, the farm-to-table trend has put a lot of variety on our plates. Think indigenous ingredients such as native greens and nuts, different ways of cooking, and a deeper understanding of India’s vast agricultural ecosystem that extends into our forests and villages.

Having said that, how often do these ingredients make their way into the mainstream culinary ecosystem? Om Routray, founder of agri-food thinktank Indian Culinary Agenda and its parent organisation, Vrihi Foundation, aims to change this with a policy report on India’s heritage produce that launched recently.
A close-up shot capturing the ripening clusters of Carissa carandas, commonly known as Karonda or Bengal currant | Photo Credit: Jayantibhai Movaliya

Covering both agriculture and forest produce, the report — created alongside The Asia Foundation and social enterprise Ekgaon — aims to not only spotlight India’s vast agricultural heritage but also proposes an operational framework with GI tagged commodity value chains, and awareness among policy makers and consumers. Elaborating on the stakeholders and researchers involved in the project, Om says that the team studied producers, processors, retailers, culinary schools, and Government agencies.

Om, who has been working on digital technologies in agriculture for a decade, talks about how the startup he worked for operated in 37 countries, but never really took off in India. “The realisation came that no matter how much we work on the agriculture side, unless we work on the complete value chain, commodity ecosystems will not be elevated as a whole. The subsequent onslaught of ingredients such as California almonds , Australian lamb, etc. also demonstrated that we are not being fair with the agro-forest heritage that we have,” he says.

The report makes a case for Indian produce such as turmeric , jamun, mahua that are ‘uniquely Indian and most are rare outside the subcontinent’. While some are GI-tagged , there is a lot that needs to be done to fully tap their potential as ‘the impact of the certification has not been uniformly beneficial and, in many instances, not equally distributed’. “Kandhamal turmeric is a great example,” says Om. “Both individual farmers and Kandhamal as a district have not benefited much from the GI tag and the constant spotlight that the commodity has brought. For instance, there are no upmarket retail stores nor any processing capacity built in the district.”

The report also spotlights the fact that most commodities are facing climate-related challenges. For instance, jamuns from Jambhulgaon in Maharashtra are facing yield and harvest issues due to unseasonal rains shifting flowering. Also, women majorly collect and process most heritage commodities and there have been very few technological interventions to remove drudgery.
Jamuns at a street market in New Delhi | Photo Credit: MelanieMaya

So, how can things change? The report makes a case for import substitution by increased utilisation of indigenous commodities by promoting them better, and bringing in a strong supply chain. Take, for instance, nuts. “We have floated the idea of a Himalayan Nuts Association that promotes indigenous nuts on the lines of California almonds. Many chefs are using jamuns instead of blueberries in cheesecakes. We have not even scratched the surface when it comes to indigenous mushrooms,” explains Om, while sharing the example of mahua syrup. “It is already seeing early adoption as a replacement for maple syrup across bakeries and restaurants. Mahua resins are a great substitution for imported resins and a similar case can be made for indigenous dry fruits.”

The report also highlights the need for diversifying India’s export basket , the bulk of which comprises rice, wheat, etc. Om says that the team has recommended two paths. “One is to de-focus from generic exports. For example, there may not be much long-term value in exporting dragon fruits from Odisha as there is no reason why global markets will perceive it as a premium product. So, we must do a terroir-culture fit before introducing new commodities in productive regions,” says Om.

fullParagraphs: India’s separation of medicine licensing under CDSCO and pricing under NPPA presents a policy challenge. Stronger coordination,supported by pharmaceutical, clinical and health-economic expertise, could bridge this gap

A cancer medicine supplied to a retailer for ₹2,700 carries a maximum retail price (MRP) of ₹27,000. Who accounts for this tenfold difference? This was among the examples highlighted by the Supreme Court in September 2026, when it questioned the gap between the prices paid for medicines and what patients ultimately pay.

Subsequently, on October 17, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) announced a 30% cap on trade margins for 137 anti-cancer drugs, effective from November 9. This intervention could reduce prices substantially for some products. It also raises a broader question: how does India decide what medicines should cost?

articles.title: Students of Wayanad school protest seeking revocation of principal’s transfer over alleged lapses during study tour
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Higher Education department took action against him claiming that official guidelines were not followed during a study tour undertaken by students

Higher secondary students of Government Higher Secondary School, Meenangadi, Wayanad, staged a protest on Monday (November 2, 2026) seeking revocation of the recent transfer of their principal Shibi Krishnan. The Higher Education department took action against him claiming that official guidelines were not followed during a study tour undertaken by the students last week.

According to reports, the sequence of events began after over 130 students went on the tour in separate buses to Hyderabad. While returning, a section of students alleged that Hajis Ulladan, the PTA president, had consumed alcohol. Videos of the PTA president in an intoxicated condition were subsequently sent to the parents through social media. Rumours spread that Mr. Krishnan too was drunk. When the students reached the school, angry parents and some political activists blocked him at the gate. Police personnel were subsequently called in, who escorted Mr. Krishnan to safety.

However, lab results of his blood samples revealed no trace of alcohol. The students who were part of the tour also came in his support, saying Mr. Krishnan had not consumed liquor and that Mr. Ulladan had been shifted to another vehicle when the complaint arose.

Meanwhile, the Regional Deputy Director of Education conducted an inquiry into the episode and found out that the school authorities had not sought permission to conduct the tour. Also, a three-day tour was reportedly extended to five days. Mr. Krishnan was subsequently transferred to Government Higher Secondary School, Vaduvanchal.

Officials of the school management committee told the media on Monday that Mr. Krishnan had been framed in the episode for political reasons. He is a leader of the pro-Left Kerala School Teachers’ Association. The officials also said that though the school authorities had sought the mandatory permission from the higher authorities, there was no response to it.

Higher secondary students of Government Higher Secondary School, Meenangadi, Wayanad, staged a protest on Monday (November 2, 2026) seeking revocation of the recent transfer of their principal Shibi Krishnan. The Higher Education department took action against him claiming that official guidelines were not followed during a study tour undertaken by the students last week.

While returning, a section of students alleged that Hajis Ulladan, the PTA president, had consumed alcohol. However, lab results of his blood samples revealed no trace of alcohol. The students who were part of the tour also came in his support, saying Mr. Krishnan had not consumed liquor and that Mr. Ulladan had been shifted to another vehicle when the complaint arose.

Meanwhile, the Regional Deputy Director of Education conducted an inquiry into the episode and found out that the school authorities had not sought permission to conduct the tour. Also, a three-day tour was reportedly extended to five days. Mr. Krishnan was subsequently transferred to Government Higher Secondary School, Vaduvanchal.

Officials of the school management committee told the media on Monday that Mr. Krishnan had been framed in the episode for political reasons. He is a leader of the pro-Left Kerala School Teachers’ Association. The officials also said that though the school authorities had sought the mandatory permission from the higher authorities, there was no response to it.

articles.title: How ‘Murasu’ became the first Tamil name for a tropical cyclone
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Murasu’ is the first Tamil name to be assigned to a tropical cyclone since the naming of cyclones over north Indian Ocean began in September 2004. ‘Murasu’ refers to a traditional Tamil percussion instrument.

A name rooted in Tamil’s cultural past is travelling across the Bay of Bengal as a weather warning. As the severe cyclonic storm advances towards the Indian coast, ‘Murasu ’ , a Tamil name suggested by the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, has found its place in the region’s meteorological history.

The storm has been named from the second list of names for tropical cyclones over the north Indian Ocean prepared by the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) panel. The traditional Tamil percussion instrument has lent its name to a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal.
A view of the Tamil percussion instrument ‘Murasu’ displayed at Thol Isai Kalanjiyam Museum at Raja Annamalai Mandram in Chennai. Representational image. File | Photo Credit: K.V. Srinivasan

S. Balachandran, former additional director general of meteorology, who was heading the RMC when the names were proposed, said ‘ Murasu ’ was the first Tamil name to be assigned to a tropical cyclone since the naming of cyclones over north Indian Ocean began in September 2004.

“We suggested names related to ocean, fish, coastal areas and communication. ‘ Murasu’ was proposed because the percussion instrument was used to disseminate information during the ancient period and to alert people about natural disasters. It also denoted a thunderous sound,” said Mr. Balachandran.

He recalled that after the names in the first list were exhausted, the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre for Tropical Cyclones over North Indian Ocean, New Delhi, sought fresh list of names from various coastal States, including Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, in 2020.

Meteorologists noted that it was the third name after ‘Gati’ and ‘Tej’ to be featured in the list of 13 names suggested by India to the WMO and United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific panel with contributions from 12 other countries. The panel met once in three years.
Initially, the names were provided by eight member countries and five more countries, including United Arab Emirates and Yemen, joined the panel for the second list of cyclone names.

articles.title: Raids on Power TV boss Rakesh Shetty’s residence, office in Bengaluru in Siddaramaiah sting video case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rakesh Shetty is a key suspect in the case and, along with expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva, is accused of being involved in the creation of the allegedly fabricated video

The Central Crime Branch (CCB) of Bengaluru police on November 2 searched the residence and office of Power TV Managing Director Rakesh Shetty in connection with the alleged fabrication and circulation of a sting video allegedly targeting former chief minister Siddaramaiah.
The searches were carried out by multiple teams of investigators after obtaining a search warrant from a court.

Rakesh Shetty is a key suspect in the case and, along with expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva , is accused of being involved in the creation of the allegedly fabricated video. Both had earlier been questioned by the police.

The searches come a day after the CCB disclosed that the mobile phone used to upload the controversial sting video had allegedly changed hands at the official residence of Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy in New Delhi.
Investigators are now seeking to establish the chain of custody of the mobile phone and the circumstances under which it was used to upload the video.

The police have issued a notice to another suspect, Prajwal Prasad, who works with the IT cell of the Janata Dal (Secular), directing him to appear for questioning. His statement is expected to be crucial in establishing how the mobile phone was procured and handed over to those allegedly involved in uploading the video.

According to the investigation, the mobile phone was allegedly handed over to Ritesh Pandey at Mr. Kumaraswamy’s official residence in New Delhi. The CCB is probing the alleged role of various individuals in the conspiracy and the subsequent circulation of the video.
The possibility of questioning Mr. Kumaraswamy or examining his official residence in Delhi will depend on the findings of the investigation and the statements of the suspects.

articles.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash case: High drama marks hearing on plea to cancel teen driver’s bail
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prosecution and counsel for victim’s family trade charges. Court says further proceedings to be held in-camera in the afternoon, considering involvement of a child in conflict with law

The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, while hearing appeals seeking the suspension of bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash in Keralam that claimed a life, witnessed high drama on Monday (November 2, 2026) as the prosecution and counsel for the victim’s family traded allegations.

Not impressed by the turn of events and the exchange of accusations, Judge Kavitha Gangadharan said that further proceedings would be held in-camera in the afternoon, considering the involvement of a child in conflict with law. The petitions will be taken up after the court finishes hearing the remaining cases listed for the day. The judge took the decision despite objections raised by the family’s counsel.
Bhadra Keerthy, daughter of the deceased Jayabalakrishnan, had told the media that the family lacked confidence in the prosecution represented by Special Public Prosecutor P.A. Bindu.

On Monday, the prosecution raised the issue before the court, accusing the victim’s family of interfering with the independent investigation through contradictory statements made to the media. Terming it a serious allegation, the judge sought clarification from the investigation officer, who had been directed by the court on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to produce the case diary on Monday, on whether such interference had indeed occurred.

M.G. Sreejith, counsel for the family, accused the prosecution of non-cooperation while denying the allegation that the victim’s family was hampering the independent investigation. The court noted that the Special Public Prosecutor had been serving in the court for seven years and observed that any grievances should have been raised before the court. The decision to conduct the proceedings in-camera came after Mr. Sreejith stated that he had certain matters to place before the court that could not be discussed in open proceedings.

The investigation officer submitted that the juvenile accused needed to be interrogated, prompting the court to ask whether moving an application before the Juvenile Justice Board would suffice for the purpose.

Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team has reportedly decided to probe the alleged destruction of evidence in the case. While hearing the criminal appeals filed by the prosecution and the victim’s family against the Juvenile Justice Board’s decision to grant bail to the 17-year-old accused, the court had directed the cyber police to remove content identifying the accused from social media and initiate action against those responsible for disseminating it.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The party questions the use of bank’s funds by Fairfax to finance acquisition; demands disclosure of valuation reports

The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

articles.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026). This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government. A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu.

“Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement. The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out.

Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi. Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the agrément (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here. India’s continued assistance to the disaster in Bhote Koshi river is also expected to be on the agenda.

Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed. Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Misri was expected to visit Nepal in May, but the visit was postponed ostensibly because Mr. Shah had prioritised domestic challenges. The India visit by Mr. Shah, if it materialises, will be the first bilateral visit abroad by the leader who came into prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising that overthrew the government of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli. Mr. Misri had visited Kathmandu previously for two days in August 2025 and had met Mr. Oli.

In the past few months, India has hosted Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who visited Delhi to participate in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) meet held on October 13, 2026. India has also hosted the head of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Rabi Lamichhane in the first week of June when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Lamichhane paid a personal visit to India last week to pray at the pilgrimage centres in Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati.

Mr. Lamichhane had described this visit as “personal and not political”. “There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” said Mr. Lamichhane before starting the visit.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 02 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026). This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government. A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu.

“Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement. The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out.

Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi. Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the agrément (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here. India’s continued assistance to the disaster in Bhote Koshi river is also expected to be on the agenda.

Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed. Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Misri was expected to visit Nepal in May, but the visit was postponed ostensibly because Mr. Shah had prioritised domestic challenges. The India visit by Mr. Shah, if it materialises, will be the first bilateral visit abroad by the leader who came into prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising that overthrew the government of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli. Mr. Misri had visited Kathmandu previously for two days in August 2025 and had met Mr. Oli.

In the past few months, India has hosted Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who visited Delhi to participate in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) meet held on October 13, 2026. India has also hosted the head of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Rabi Lamichhane in the first week of June when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Lamichhane paid a personal visit to India last week to pray at the pilgrimage centres in Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati.

Mr. Lamichhane had described this visit as “personal and not political”. “There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” said Mr. Lamichhane before starting the visit.

articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed good faith

Iran on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as U.S. President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.
A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed "good faith".

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.
"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.
"We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period."

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz if the U.S. agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

During final rallies for the U.S. midterms on Tuesday (November 3), where diesel prices and consumer inflation are a key issue, Trump struck a belligerent tone, warning Iran to expect "the hammer".

"The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can... But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer," he told voters in Iowa.
Officials from Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey have held talks with Iran in recent days, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Tehran.

articles.title: U.K. warns EU against keeping Britain out of ‘Made in Europe’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The European Union wants to boost domestic sectors like cars and defence by forcing companies to buy European if they want public money
U.K. Defence Minister Wes Streeting on Monday (November 1, 2026) warned the EU against keeping Britain out of its "Made in Europe" industrial push, weeks before a key EU-U.K. summit.

The European Union wants to boost domestic sectors like cars and defence by forcing companies to buy European if they want public money, but the efforts have raised concerns in London about the U.K.'s potential exclusion.

"We need to be careful" to avoid that the Made in Europe push "doesn't spread into self-defeating protectionism", Streeting said alongside top EU diplomat Kaja Kallas ahead of their talks in Brussels.
The British Minister will also meet EU Defence Chief Andrius Kubilius.
Monday's (November 2) talks come just over two weeks before EU chiefs and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet for a summit in Brussels on November 20.
Mr. Burnham has said the long-awaited meeting would be a chance to start a "serious dialogue" about long-term relations between the U.K. and the bloc, a decade after the Brexit vote to leave.
One of the major issues on the table this month will be "Made in Europe" even though it is not officially on the summit's agenda.

As the EU's push to cut dependence on non-EU companies widens to include artificial intelligence development and cloud computing, the U.K. fears new digital rules being prepared will also exclude British companies.
London and Brussels hope to clinch deals on food and drink trade, youth mobility and avoiding EU carbon emissions taxes during the November 20 talks.
The EU hopes to make progress especially on cutting the fees EU students have to pay to attend British universities.

articles.title: Ebola reminder of urgent need to finish pandemic treaty: WHO chief
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people"
Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday.
Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice.
As the ninth meeting towards finalising the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to "finish the job".
Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people".
"A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country," he said, according to a written version of his statement.
"The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat."

He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC.
It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: "no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone".
When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line.

The agreement's Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments.

articles.title: Vietnam scraps child organ donors proposal after backlash
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The newly revised draft still allows living minors to donate regenerative tissue, for bone marrow or stem cell transplants, to family members when no suitable adult donor is available
Vietnam withdrew on Monday a proposal allowing children aged 15 to 17 to donate their organs after death following public criticism in a country where deceased donor transplants remain limited.
The Southeast Asian country began kidney transplants in 1992 and performs the most annual transplants in the region, according to state media.
However, the vast majority of transplants in Vietnam rely on living donors. Transplants in many other nations mostly use organs from deceased donors, expanding their donor pool.
Officials in Vietnam say they are seeking to update a 2006 law on organ and tissue donation, aiming to increase life-saving transplants while safeguarding donors.

A draft submitted to the National Assembly last month proposed allowing 15- to 17-year-olds to donate their tissues, organs or bodies after death, provided the child's parent or legal representative consented.

But, after online backlash, officials removed the under-18 donor provision from a revised draft dated Sunday, with the government saying it had accepted recommendations from lawmakers that only legal adults should be permitted to donate their organs.
Dissent is heavily restricted in communist Vietnam, but opposition centred on whether parental consent could adequately protect child donors from pressure or exploitation.
Criticism also focused on a survey of schoolchildren as young as seven conducted in October to gather feedback on the draft law.
The poll prompted questions about whether minors could understand complex medical, legal and ethical issues, state outlet Tuoi Tre News said.
It said "the provision allowing minors to register as posthumous organ donors prompted considerable controversy and differing opinions among the public".

The newly revised draft still allows living minors to donate regenerative tissue, for bone marrow or stem cell transplants, to family members when no suitable adult donor is available

Vietnam withdrew on Monday a proposal allowing children aged 15 to 17 to donate their organs after death following public criticism in a country where deceased donor transplants remain limited.

The Southeast Asian country began kidney transplants in 1992 and performs the most annual transplants in the region, according to state media.

However, the vast majority of transplants in Vietnam rely on living donors. Transplants in many other nations mostly use organs from deceased donors, expanding their donor pool.

Officials in Vietnam say they are seeking to update a 2006 law on organ and tissue donation, aiming to increase life-saving transplants while safeguarding donors.

A draft submitted to the National Assembly last month proposed allowing 15- to 17-year-olds to donate their tissues, organs or bodies after death, provided the child's parent or legal representative consented.

But, after online backlash, officials removed the under-18 donor provision from a revised draft dated Sunday, with the government saying it had accepted recommendations from lawmakers that only legal adults should be permitted to donate their organs.

Dissent is heavily restricted in communist Vietnam, but opposition centred on whether parental consent could adequately protect child donors from pressure or exploitation.

Criticism also focused on a survey of schoolchildren as young as seven conducted in October to gather feedback on the draft law.

The poll prompted questions about whether minors could understand complex medical, legal and ethical issues, state outlet Tuoi Tre News said.

It said "the provision allowing minors to register as posthumous organ donors prompted considerable controversy and differing opinions among the public".

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Police probe alleged exploitation of 43 women, including possible forged consent documents and illegal commissions, while examining recruitment networks, payment trails and the role of IVF and fertility centres in Hyderabad

Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.

The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.

The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.

The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.

Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The study’s findings about women having a higher prevalence of pain across anatomical sites, resonate with observations from India, say experts, noting that even so, women’s pain has historically been under-recognised, misunderstood, or inadequately treated

Women are more likely than men to report pain across every one of the 11 anatomical sites examined in a global study involving more than 6.1 million people across 118 countries. The study found that differences were particularly pronounced for facial pain, headaches and abdominal pain.

Published in Nature Medicine , the study found that women had 83% higher relative prevalence of facial pain, 74% higher prevalence of headaches and 60% higher prevalence of stomach or abdominal pain than men. Women were also more likely to report high-intensity and widespread pain, highlighting a disparity that extends beyond the occurrence of pain to its severity and distribution.

articles.title: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max Review | One of this season’s best Android flagships
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The triple-200MP cameras are its biggest strength, while the Dimensity 9600 Pro and ColorOS 17 make it a complete package

Oppo has consistently pushed the boundaries of smartphone innovation with its flagship Find X series. Earlier this year, the Find X9 Ultra raised the bar for mobile photography . Now, the brand is back with the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max: a flagship that blurs the line between the Find X9 Pro and Find X9 Ultra. Yet, after spending time with it, I feel the X10 Pro Max deserves to stand on its own.

At first glance, the phone bears a striking resemblance to the Find X9 Pro. However, its camera system tells a very different story. With three 200MP rear cameras, the Find X10 Pro Max takes smartphone photography to an entirely new level. It also packs flagship-grade performance, a premium design and features that justify its position at the very top of Oppo’s lineup.

But this comes at a price of ₹1,99,999. The Find X10 Pro Max is among the most expensive conventional smartphones on the market, making it a serious investment for anyone who wants the best Android has to offer. So, does Oppo’s latest flagship deliver enough to justify its premium positioning? And more importantly, is the Find X10 Pro Max the best flagship smartphone of the season? Let’s find out.

The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max comes in two variants: Titanium Grey and Lumos White. My review unit is the Titanium Grey version. It feels understated and premium. The Lumos White variant is slightly lighter and features a textured glass back. My unit, however, misses both the Hasselblad branding and the textured finish. The rest of the design remains largely identical.

The phone is big and wide, measuring 161.32mm in height and 76.57mm in width. At 235g, it has considerable heft. However, the weight distribution keeps it balanced in the hand. Oppo has retained the separate camera and flash modules, which make the phone slightly top-heavy. Unlike the Find X9 Ultra, though, the X10 Pro Max does not wear its camera credentials so boldly. The Ultra’s massive circular camera island made photography its design identity. Here, Oppo takes a more restrained approach.

The metal frame adds to the premium feel, while the flat edges make the device easier to grip. The right side houses the power and volume buttons, while the left gets the customisable Snap Key. The bottom includes the USB-C port, SIM tray, microphone and speaker. The Snap Key is useful for quickly accessing functions such as the flashlight, recorder or AI Mind Space. However, I would have liked more customisation options for shortcuts.

Turn the phone around, and the front looks equally premium. The large display is surrounded by slim, symmetrical bezels, creating an immersive viewing experience. The phone also carries IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings for dust and water resistance. This reassures the owners of a device that costs nearly ₹2,00,000.
Overall, the design feels refined rather than radical, and that works in its favour.

The Find X10 Pro Max features a 6.78-inch AMOLED display with a 2772 x 1272-pixel resolution. It supports an adaptive refresh rate of up to 120Hz, with 144Hz available in supported games. Scrolling feels fluid, animations remain smooth, and the screen responds quickly to touch. The display also supports 10-bit colour, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision. This makes it an excellent choice for watching movies, editing photographs and gaming.

Brightness reaches 2,000 nits in high-brightness mode, while the panel supports 3,840Hz PWM dimming. The display remains vibrant and comfortable across different lighting conditions. Compared with the Find X9 Pro, the X10 Pro Max brings a higher gaming refresh rate. However, the Find X9 Ultra still offers a sharper 3168 x 1440 resolution. For everyday users, the X10 Pro Max delivers a rich and immersive display.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Cost of input materials increased 20% during the quarter.
Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: With Deepavali falling in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to begin shopping after receiving their monthly salaries and festival bonuses; the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is likely to witness massive retail activity
Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: In his first visit, BJP’s Bihar in-charge Harish Dwivedi stresses on strengthening the party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dwivedi gave guidance on strengthening the organisation through regular meetings and effective public outreach campaigns

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National General Secretary and Bihar in-charge, Harish Dwivedi, on Saturday (October 31, 2026) made his first visit to the State and directed the party workers and leaders to make organisational tasks more effective and to ensure that the government’s achievements are communicated to the public through the party’s network.

He also convened an organisational meeting of State office-bearers at the Atal Auditorium in the BJP state office. The meeting was attended by Bihar co-in-charges and National Secretaries Rohan Gupta and Sangeeta Yadav.
Bihar BJP State President Sanjay Saraogi, Organisational General Secretary Bhikhubhai Dalsania, National Secretary Siddharth Shambhu, and other state-level office-bearers were also present.
According to the party sources, Mr. Dwivedi spoke to the State office-bearers and discussed current activities, future action plans, and ways to further strengthen the party.

In the meeting, it was also decided to accelerate organizational activities by holding regular meetings at the Morcha, Mandal, and booth levels. Mr. Dwivedi pointed out the necessity for office-bearers and party workers to undertake regular visits, noting that such visits allow for an assessment of the organization’s actual status.
“This facilitates direct communication with party workers and helps in resolving organisational issues,”Mr. Dwivedi said.

Mr. Saraogi on the other hand said that the BJP has grown strong through the hard work, dedication, and commitment to public service shown by its workers. He asserted that the active participation of all office-bearers and workers—from the state level down to the booth level is essential for the organisation’s strength.

He reiterated that the party’s top priority is to ensure that the government’s welfare schemes and achievements reach the last person in society, adding that all office-bearers must work in close coordination to achieve this.

It was decided in the meeting that all state-level office-bearers would conduct organisational visits in accordance with a prescribed action plan. During these visits, meetings will be held at the mandal and booth levels to engage with party workers. Additionally, the organisation’s programmes will be reviewed, and preparations will be made for upcoming activities.

Mr. Saraogi said that all office-bearers would work with full commitment to strengthen the organisation and communicate the government’s achievements to the general public. He added that the BJP’s objective is to make the organisation more active, empowered, and people-oriented.

articles.title: Madras High Court Advocates Association challenges 1965 Union Cabinet decision to continue English as common language for Supreme Court and all High Courts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Says, the 1965 decision came to its notice only in 2025 pursuant to details obtained by a lawyer under the Right to Information Act, 2005

The Madras High Court Advocates Association (MHAA) has filed a public interest litigation petition in the High Court challenging the constitutional validity of an Union Cabinet Committee’s 1965 decision that English should continue as the common language for the Supreme Court and all High Courts in the country until it could be replaced with Hindi.

First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan would be hearing the case on Monday (November 2, 2026). MHAA has contended that the bar imposed on use of regional languages in High Courts violates Articles 14 (right to equality), 19 (freedom of speech and expression) and 21 (right to life) of the Constitution.

In his affidavit MHAA secretary S. Arivazhagan said, the association came to know about the 1965 Cabinet decision only last year from an advocate who had obtained the details under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 and hence it had chosen to challenge it now. The assocation did not want the Cabinet decision to hamper the long pending demand to make Tamil as the official language of Madras High Court.

MHAA said, a conference of Chief Justices of all High Courts in the country was held in the first week of March 1965 under the chairmanship of the then Chief Justice of India (CJI) P.B. Gajendragadkar. The resolutions passed in the conference were not released to the press but they were forwarded to Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, Union Home Minister Gulzarilal Nanda and all Chief Ministers on March 26, 1965.

The CJI’s letter to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) stated that the conference had recommended that the Supreme Court and all High Courts should have a common language, English should continue to be such common language “until in due course Hindi becomes rich and ripe enough to take its place” and that regional languages should not be introduced as languages of High Courts.

Subsequently, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) put up a note before the Cabinet Committee, constituted to consider different aspects of regional language policy, on May 17, 1965. The note read that there would be difficulty in elevating High Court judges to the Supreme Court and also in the appearance of lawyers before various High Courts and the Supreme Court if there was no common language for these courts.

“One of the major unifying factors in the country is a unified judicial system with a common language and uniform way of functioning in High Courts. Nothing should be done that is likely to weaken the present system. There can be little doubt that if regional languages were permitted to be used in the High Courts, we would be moving towards fragmentation of the judicial system, and it would not be possible to maintain for long the unitary character of the judicial system with the Supreme Court at the apex. An all-India bar of any sort cannot also continue to exist,” the note read.

The MHA said, the Cabinet may accept the recommendation of the Chief Justices’ conference that the Supreme Court and all the High Courts in the country should have a common language and that English should continue to be used until Hindi could take its place.

On Article 348(2) of the Constitution which empowers the Governors, with the previous consent of the President, to authorise the use of regional languages in the High Court proceedings (but for judgements, decrees or orders passed by the court), the MHA said, the President would be justified in denying consent since the CJI as well as the Chief Justices of the High Courts were opposed to introduction of regional languages.

“It might also be desirable to adopt a convention whereby the CJI would be consulted before the President gave his consent to any such proposal,” the MHA note read. The Cabinet Committee considered the note and approved it on May 21, 1965.

articles.title: Akhilesh pitches Gorakhpur vs Kashi narrative, eyes inroads among Brahmins, business community
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Akhilesh Yadav is attempting to make inroads among Brahmins and the Bania community by accusing the Chief Minister and his regime of being anti-Brahmins and Banias

After the results of the Legislative Council polls, the Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav is trying to pitch an alleged disagreement between the central leadership and the state leadership of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by projecting a Gorakhpur versus Varanasi plank.
He is attempting to make inroads among Brahmins and the Bania community by accusing the Chief Minister and his regime of being anti-Brahmins and Banias.

“Let Kashi drown, but our Gorakhpur business must not stop,” said Mr. Yadav, in a reference to the BJP victory in the Gorakhpur Legislative Council Graduates’ seat, alleging the victory at the cost of the party losing both Legislative Council seats in the Varanasi region.

“The BJP has victimised, oppressed, and humiliated every community, so all the oppressed have come together. The PDA’s support base has now reached 95%, thanks to the Brahmin community, the business community, and the Kayastha community voting for us. For the BJP, politics, not community, is paramount. They’ve resorted to every tactic to defeat their traditional voting communities. The BJP is not anyone’s ally. That’s why, whether it’s the Brahmin community, the business community, or the Kayastha community, everyone is now with us. That’s why we’re now at 95%,” said Mr. Yadav on Friday (October 30, 2026), in Lucknow, addressing a meeting attended by Legislative Council winners from the party and candidates.
In another outreach to Brahmins, Mr. Yadav said the entire Brahmin community is witnessing the harassment of Sanjayan Tripathi, the SP candidate from Gorakhpur Graduates’ seat.

“Corrupt BJP members and their conspiring allies and complicit officials have stooped to every level to win the MLC election. The conspiracy to defeat Dr. Sanjayan Tripathi has been exposed for all to see. The reason for defeating Dr. Sanjayan Tripathi by rigging the counting of votes is not just that he is the SP candidate, but the main reason behind it is ‘Haata Nahi Bhaata’,” he said.

“The BJP has gone downhill in politics. After such a massive fraud, the public has come to understand that the BJP has actually lost every seat. The entire community is witnessing the harassment Dr. Sanjayan Tripathi has faced. His community and the state’s teachers will never forget Dr. Tripathi’s tears,” he added.
The SP won five out of 11 Council seats, which went to the polls on October 23, while the BJP emerged victorious in six seats.

When explicitly asked about the meaning of ‘Haata Nahi Bhaata’, the SP spokesperson Sunil Singh Yadav ‘Sajan’, said, “It is well-known that Haata represents the late Hari Shankar Tiwari, a senior leader from Gorakhpur hailing from the Brahmin community, who is not liked by the present CM. Not only the late Tiwari Ji and his family, but Brahmins in general are not liked by the CM, his hatred towards the community reflects in his government’s approach towards Brahmins”.

Downplaying any resentment over leadership or within the party, the Union Home Minister, in his speech at the BJP’s State executive meeting, urged party workers to throw disappointment and resentment into the Gomti river and work with dedication to form the BJP government for the third time.

articles.title: Devotees worried over conduct of Kandasashti festival at Kandakottam temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devotees of the Sri Muthukumaraswamy Temple, popularly known as Kandhakottam in Rattan Bazaar in Park Town, are worried about the conduct of the Kandasashti festival this year.

"Usually, tickets for the Laksharcharnai during the annual festival are sold just after Vijayadasami. Till date, the administration has not started selling tickets. Every year around 35,000 tickets each priced at ₹300 are sold to devotees who want to participate in the archanai that is slated to start on November 10. There is no sign of the conduct of the festival so far," said A. B. Srinivasan, a 65-year-old devotee.

Saravanan, another devotee, said that this year would be the 99 th consecutive year of the Kandasashti festival during which grand concerts would be held. "Participants of the archanai would be given prasadam, including a bucket. Tenders for procuring various items, such as pandals, coconuts, bags, and flowers are yet to be called for. We hear that the executive officer has gone on leave and another person has taken charge," he said.

The over 500-year-old shrine, is a scheme temple, meaning it belongs to a particular community — in this case, the Berri Chettis. A five-member team was chosen from the community as trustees last year and they have also been in charge of the daily administration of the temple.

Sendilvellan, one of the trustees, said that the executive officer had taken away cheque signatory powers from the trustees and the trustees were unable to pay even salaries. "He has gone to the bank and taken signatory powers without informing us. We seem to have absolutely no powers in the day-to-day running of the temple. The court had directed the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department to interfere only if there was any problem relating to the conduct of the temple. From last year, we have been managing the temple without any problems," he said.

Another trustee said that with just a few days left for the festival they have been running from pillar to post trying to get the powers back and conduct it. Sources in the HR&CE Department said they would look into the matter.

articles.title: We did not buy peace; we established peace in J&K: L-G Manoj Sinha on UT Foundation Day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: L-G Manoj Sinha said terror, separatism and stone-pelting have given way to democracy, development and public participation after Article 370 was removed

J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, while speaking on the 8th J&K Union Territory Foundation Day and the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, said Article 370’s abrogation gave ordinary citizens freedom from fear and access to rights denied for decades. However, no ruling party leader or Minister attended the function on the foundation day. “We did not buy peace; we established peace. Zero-tolerance policy crippled terror networks and restored normal life across J&K. Since 2020, more than 780 terrorists have been eliminated, local recruitment ended, stone-pelting erased. Now Jammu Kashmir is witnessing a historic security transformation.” He said terror, separatism and stone-pelting have given way to democracy, development and public participation after Article 370 was removed. “Strong action against narco-terrorism continues. We have arrested thousands of drug smugglers and drug peddlers this year. Their illicit assets have been attached, and drug-funded mansions were demolished. Conflict entrepreneurs who profited from separatism and terrorism stand exposed. People of J&K have embraced peace, progress and national integration,” said Mr. Sinha. Terming October 31 “not merely a date”, Mr. Sinha said, “It is a milestone that changed the direction of history and strengthened the spirit of national integration, equality and inclusive development. Article 370 abrogation gave ordinary citizens freedom from fear and access to rights denied for decades. J&K has emerged as a model of peace, development and good governance,” said Mr. Sinha. Referring to the aspirations of the people, Mr. Sharma said that the future of J&K must be shaped by peace, equal opportunities and development. “The future of Jammu and Kashmir lies not in the shadow of terror, but in the light of peace; not behind the walls of discrimination, but in equal opportunities; and not in stagnation, but in the momentum of progress,” he added. The Lieutenant Governor emphasised that unity is sustained through justice and public trust. “Public trust must be won not merely by promises, but by deeds. Justice and accountability are the strongest foundations of unity,” he said. Mr. Sinha underlined the need to ensure that growth remains inclusive and reaches every household, village and community. “Children and youth are growing up in an environment focused on education, opportunity and progress, enabling them to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. A stable and peaceful environment benefits every section of society, including farmers, entrepreneurs, traders, students and workers,” said Mr. Sinha. He expressed satisfaction that the people of J&K were increasingly participating in developmental initiatives and contributing to the region’s growth story. “My dream is that by 2047, J&K should emerge as a model of prosperity with a modern economy, world-class healthcare, excellent education and a vibrant cultural heritage,” said Mr. Sinha. Meanwhile, a documentary film on J&K’s transformational journey was also screened. The function was attended by senior BJP leader and chairperson, J&K Waqf Board, Dr. Syed Darakhshan Andrabi; Chief Secretary, Atal Dulloo; Director General of Police, Nalin Prabhat, etc. However, no leader from the regional parties, including the ruling National Conference, attended these functions. Meanwhile, speaking on the ‘Rashtriya Ekta Diwas’, Mr. Sinha administered the ‘Unity Pledge’ to Lok Bhavan officials, staff and security personnel.
