articles.title: Slovakian couple had come for a holiday to India, man died hours after checking into Conrad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Wife says that she rushed to check on him after hearing a loud noise from near the pool, but found him motionless in the water.

A holiday in India turned tragic for a Slovakian couple, as the man ended up being electrocuted to death in a swimming pool at Hotel Conrad, a five-star hotel in central Bengaluru, hours after they checked into the hotel on October 30, Friday.
Silvia Hotuatova, 47, told the police that she, along with her husband Juraj Horvat, 45, had arrived in India on October 20 for a holiday and they checked into the hotel on October 30.

Hours later, at around 5.15 p.m., Mr. Horvat went swimming in the hotel’s pool, his wife told the police. She said that she rushed to check on him after hearing a loud noise from near the pool, but found him motionless in the water.

“When hotel staff attempted to rescue him, they too sustained injuries. Another person noticed an electric current in the pool, following which the hotel staff immediately switched off the power supply. Matthew Phelan, an American national, attempted to rescue the victims and administer cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The victims were subsequently shifted to a hospital in an ambulance,” she told the police.

Manipal Hospital said four people were brought on Friday evening. One of them, Mr. Horvat, was reportedly brought to the hospital in a state of cardiac arrest, following which the emergency team immediately initiated CPR and resuscitation. Despite continued efforts and all clinical measures, the patient could not be revived and was declared dead.

The second individual, a German national in his early 40s, was brought to the hospital with no signs of life and was declared “brought dead”, according to the statement. The German national, identified as Alexander Maximilian Theiss, 57, a Lufthansa Airlines crew member, was reportedly part of an airline crew that had arrived in Bengaluru from Frankfurt and were staying at the hotel during a break in their flight schedule. The incident has reportedly left other members of the airline crew and hotel staff traumatised.

A statement from Manipal Hospital further said that during the incident, a 26-year-old Conrad staff member entered the water in an attempt to rescue the German national and the other individual. He was subsequently brought to the hospital in a state of shock, and is currently stable and under observation.

A U.S. national in his early 40s, who was also in the pool at the time, realised that there was a strong current in the water, and managed to swim to safety. He was subsequently brought to the hospital with a headache and in a state of shock. He is currently stable and under observation.

articles.title: London police arrest 139 people outside U.S. Embassy for supporting banned pro-Palestinian group
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Many of those protesting were retirees and were holding signs reading: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action”
London police said they arrested 139 people at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in support of the banned group Palestine Action.

The majority of those taken into custody had expressed support for a proscribed organisation, London's Metropolitan Police said in a statement. It said that more arrests are expected as officers remain at the scene.

Many of those protesting were retirees and were holding signs reading: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.” One protester climbed a tree outside the embassy and could be seen waving a placard reading “God help us. Teachers who support Palestine. Palestine Action.”
More than 4,000 people have been detained since July 2025 for defying the ban, said Defend Our Juries, an activist organisation that planned the demonstration.

“It is truly dystopian that there have now been over 4,000 arrests under terror laws for peaceful vigils silently expressing opposition to genocide and support for the protest group Palestine Action,” the group said.

The U.K. government outlawed the direct-action protest group last year as a terrorist organisation. The ban makes membership in or support for Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

Demonstrators also held a vigil in support of Palestine Action outside the U.S. Consulate in Edinburgh, Scotland, holding placards akin to those in London. No arrests were reported there, but Police Scotland said that inquiries to identify people seen wearing T-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organisation were ongoing.
“Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate," it said.

The protests came before an appeal on November 4 at the Supreme Court against Palestine Action's designation as a terror group. Supporters say the ban is draconian and that it violates their freedom of speech.
In August, the U.S. government announced sanctions against Palestine Action, designating it as a terror group.

Many of those protesting were retirees and were holding signs reading: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action”

London police said they arrested 139 people at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in support of the banned group Palestine Action.

The majority of those taken into custody had expressed support for a proscribed organisation, London's Metropolitan Police said in a statement. It said that more arrests are expected as officers remain at the scene.

Many of those protesting were retirees and were holding signs reading: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.” One protester climbed a tree outside the embassy and could be seen waving a placard reading “God help us. Teachers who support Palestine. Palestine Action.”

More than 4,000 people have been detained since July 2025 for defying the ban, said Defend Our Juries, an activist organisation that planned the demonstration.

“It is truly dystopian that there have now been over 4,000 arrests under terror laws for peaceful vigils silently expressing opposition to genocide and support for the protest group Palestine Action,” the group said.

The U.K. government outlawed the direct-action protest group last year as a terrorist organisation. The ban makes membership in or support for Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison.

Demonstrators also held a vigil in support of Palestine Action outside the U.S. Consulate in Edinburgh, Scotland, holding placards akin to those in London. No arrests were reported there, but Police Scotland said that inquiries to identify people seen wearing T-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organisation were ongoing.

“Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate," it said.

The protests came before an appeal on November 4 at the Supreme Court against Palestine Action's designation as a terror group. Supporters say the ban is draconian and that it violates their freedom of speech.

In August, the U.S. government announced sanctions against Palestine Action, designating it as a terror group.

articles.title: Rubio says U.S. not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in the October 25 run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on October 28
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that Washington was not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s arrangements to leave Brazil after his election loss.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after a court ordered his passports be seized amid multiple investigations against him.

“He had previously held a visa, and the President made a decision to allow him to enter the country,” Mr. Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he hosted G20 Foreign Ministers for a two-day meeting.
But Mr. Rubio added that “the U.S. government was not involved directly” in arrangements Mr. Bolsonaro made to leave his country.

Following the vote, the 45-year-old bolted from Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador in a plane that some U.S. media, including The New York Times and The Wall Street Journa l, reported was chartered by Jason Miller, an adviser to U.S. President Donald Trump.
The plane that whisked the Mr. Bolsonaro family to the United States was paid for by an intermediary from a U.S. bank account, the head of the airline has told AFP .
The White House has not commented on the flight, but Mr. Trump has called the Brazilian election “disgraceful.”

A Brazilian diplomatic source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that Argentina’s diplomatic representative had been summoned for a “routine meeting” to “provide explanations” on the flight.
Argentina’s Foreign Minister later denied that Brazil had asked Buenos Aires to explain its role in the operation.
Since arriving in the U.S., Mr. Bolsonaro has claimed to be the true leader of Brazil and said that he left the country because he was a victim of “persecution.”

articles.title: IIT Bombay student death: Parents seek CBI investigation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The petition alleged that police had failed to probe the case with the seriousness it merits and, hence, sought the probe to be monitored by a retired judge

Ravindra C. Wakode and Sonali Wakode have filed a petition in the Bombay High Court seeking transfer of the investigation into the death of their son, Sahil Wakode, to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or a Special Investigation Team (SIT). The petition seeks supervision of the investigation by a judge who has retired from the High Court.

The petition, filed through advocate Hitendra Gandhi, states that the Powai police registered a case of abetment of suicide. The parents state that the police have not investigated the role of authorities of the institute. The petition seeks directions to secure all CCTV footage from September 18, 2026, and to prevent contact with witnesses.

Sahil Wakode, 20, was a student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering. On September 18, 2026, during an examination, Prof. Suryanarayan Doolla, who was the instructor and an invigilator, removed Sahil from the hall. The petition states that Prof. Doolla took Sahil to the office of the Head of the Department.

The petition refers to the ‘Procedures for handling acts of academic malpractice by students’ from April 2015. The rules state that an invigilator should confiscate material, issue an answer book and allow the student to continue the examination. The petition states that Prof. Doolla did not follow this procedure. The parents allege that Sahil was questioned and asked to write a letter to apologise.

Sahil Wakode died on September 18, 2026. The petition states that the police declined to register an FIR. The police registered F.I.R. No. 999 of 2026 on September 19, 2026, under Sections 108 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. The investigation was transferred to the Crime Branch.

The parents seek an investigation into the actions of the authorities. The petition states that the actions of the authorities amount to abetment of suicide under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Those in distress may contact Sanjivini, Society for Mental Health suicide prevention helpline: 011-40769002.

articles.title: Ajay Devgn moves Bombay High Court against FDA notice over Vimal Elaichi advertisements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The FDA said on October 30 that its proceedings against three actors had ended and that the matter would go before the Joint Commissioner for adjudication
Actor Ajay Devgn has moved the Bombay High Court against a show-cause notice from the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration over his appearance in Vimal Elaichi advertisements

The FDA said on Friday (October 30, 2026) that its proceedings against three actors had ended and that the matter would go before the Joint Commissioner for adjudication. The High Court may hear Mr. Devgn’s petition on November 4.

The FDA issued show-cause notices to Mr. Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August. The department alleged that their advertisements for Vimal Elaichi promoted Vimal Pan Masala. The department linked the brand to the sale of gutkha and pan masala, products the State does not allow.

FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe told the media at a press conference on Friday (October 30, 2026) that the proceedings had been closed and that the Designated Officer was proposing adjudication before the Joint Commissioner. He said the Joint Commissioner was the authority to adjudicate the case.
Mr. Mundhe said the adjudication proceedings may be heard by next week. The department would continue its proceedings before the Joint Commissioner, he said.

Mr. Devgn’s petition, states that the FDA served the notice on him as an actor and not on the company that manufactures the product. The petition also challenges the validity under the Constitution of provisions of the Food Safety Regulations. Mr. Devgn has contended that he should be excused from the proceedings as he is no longer associated with the brand.

On September 14, the Delhi High Court refused to entertain a plea against the show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra FDA to the three actors. The court dismissed a plea by PB Agro LLP, a licensee for the manufacture and sale of elaichi and pan masala not containing tobacco under the Vimal brand. The Delhi High Court observed that courts in Maharashtra were the forum for such a challenge. Mr. Devgn then approached the Bombay High Court.
A division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna may hear the petition on November 4.

The FDA said on October 30 that its proceedings against three actors had ended and that the matter would go before the Joint Commissioner for adjudication

Actor Ajay Devgn has moved the Bombay High Court against a show-cause notice from the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration over his appearance in Vimal Elaichi advertisements

The FDA said on Friday (October 30, 2026) that its proceedings against three actors had ended and that the matter would go before the Joint Commissioner for adjudication. The High Court may hear Mr. Devgn’s petition on November 4.

The FDA issued show-cause notices to Mr. Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August. The department alleged that their advertisements for Vimal Elaichi promoted Vimal Pan Masala. The department linked the brand to the sale of gutkha and pan masala, products the State does not allow.

FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe told the media at a press conference on Friday (October 30, 2026) that the proceedings had been closed and that the Designated Officer was proposing adjudication before the Joint Commissioner. He said the Joint Commissioner was the authority to adjudicate the case.

Mr. Mundhe said the adjudication proceedings may be heard by next week. The department would continue its proceedings before the Joint Commissioner, he said.

Mr. Devgn’s petition, states that the FDA served the notice on him as an actor and not on the company that manufactures the product. The petition also challenges the validity under the Constitution of provisions of the Food Safety Regulations. Mr. Devgn has contended that he should be excused from the proceedings as he is no longer associated with the brand.

On September 14, the Delhi High Court refused to entertain a plea against the show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra FDA to the three actors. The court dismissed a plea by PB Agro LLP, a licensee for the manufacture and sale of elaichi and pan masala not containing tobacco under the Vimal brand. The Delhi High Court observed that courts in Maharashtra were the forum for such a challenge. Mr. Devgn then approached the Bombay High Court.

A division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna may hear the petition on November 4.

articles.title: IOA’s election Code of Conduct bars criticism of ‘private life’ of candidates, publicity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The election to pick 10 members of the Athletes' Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will be held on November 3, while the polls to choose eight SOMs will be held on November 9

No criticism of opponents’ “private lives”, a bar on all forms of publicity, including the use of new media and social networks, and a requirement for IOA and NSF office-bearers to maintain neutrality feature in the Model Code of Conduct for the upcoming elections to the Athletes’ Commission and Sportspersons of Merit (SOMs).

The election to pick 10 members of the Athletes' Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will be held on November 3, while the polls to choose eight SOMs will be held on November 9. Both elections will be held virtually, and separate instructions will be issued later by Electoral Officer Sanjay Kumar Srivastava.

There are 12 candidates — including Olympic medallists P.V. Sindhu and Mirabai Chanu — in the fray for the Athletes' Commission membership. The 10 members — five men and five women — will be elected by the 34 members of the electoral college — two each from 17 National Sports Federations (NSFs).
Eight SOMs — four men and four women — will be elected from among 80 SOMs — 40 men and 40 women — notified by the Electoral Officer.
Some of the legendary figures of Indian sports, including incumbent IOA President P.T. Usha, are in the fray to become one of the eight SOMs.

"A candidate shall not produce any spoken word, written text or representation of any nature likely to harm the image of another candidate or cause him prejudice, and criticism of other candidates, if made, shall be confined to their policies and programme, past record and work," one of the provisions of the Model Code of Conduct said.

"The promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks, and no public meeting or gathering of any kind may be organised in the process of promoting a candidature.”

"NSF and candidates shall refrain from criticism of all aspects of private life, not connected with the public activities of the athletes. No candidate shall engage in criticism based on unverified allegations or distortion against any other candidate, and there shall be no appeal to caste or communal feelings for securing votes."
The Model Code of Conduct also prescribed that electoral campaigns shall be carried out by the candidates in a fair manner and, in a spirit of respect for fundamental ethical principles.
"Candidates shall conduct all campaigns with dignity and moderation and with respect for any other candidates, the National Sports Body and its members.”

articles.title: Rubio says U.S. yet to decide on new Iran strikes
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Iran’s supreme leader October 31, 2026 warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections
U.S. President Donald Trump has not decided on fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
“We can achieve military objectives if we seek to,” Mr. Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was hosting G20 foreign ministers for a two-day meeting.
But Mr. Rubio added that Mr. Trump “hasn’t made a decision” on further military action, amid reports that the U.S. leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).
“I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Mr. Rubio said.
While he slammed Tehran for “actively and openly” targeting commercial vessels for attack, Mr. Rubio also expressed Mr. Trump’s preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran.
“I’m not going to characterise neither the progress on those talks nor any timeframe on it, other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” Mr. Rubio said.
Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday (October 31, 2026) warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections.
Mr. Trump earlier warned of the potential for fresh military action after U.S. midterms, saying previously that he was weighing up whether to “finish them off.”
But any further attack would spark concern among U.S. allies.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP : “We are calling for a diplomatic solution, and really, escalation does not benefit anyone.”

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls

CPI(M) MP John Brittas on Sunday (November 1, 2026) described the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan as a landmark protest that would have a major impact on the country’s politics. He claimed that more than 10 lakh people would gather and said the ground was already packed before the event began.

Mr. Brittas said the rally would send a strong message to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, demanding the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He warned that the government should act on the demand or face further political consequences.

Congress leader Pawan Khera said “this is the calm before the storm”, adding that the “coming storm will sweep Gyanesh away” and that Amit Shah and Narendra Modi would also “not remain in their positions”.

articles.title: Global criticism during COVID-19 hardened China’s attitude towards world: Foreign Secretary Misri
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Misri also recalled that he faced a major challenge during his posting in China as Ambassador, when India and China had an unprecedented confrontation in eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said that during COVID-19 , China felt blamed and stigmatised by the international community for the pandemic, leading to a harsh attitude toward the outside world and a draconian lockdown within its borders.
Speaking on Saturday (October 31, 2026) at the Iqwat Global Business Conclave, an event organised by an association of Kashmiri Pandits.
Mr. Misri also recalled that he faced a major challenge during his posting in China as Ambassador , when India and China had an unprecedented confrontation in eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley.
“For the first time in nearly 50 years, lives were lost on both sides at the Line of Actual Control,” he noted.

“What made it particularly challenging was that it happened at the height of COVID-19, which imposed limitations on interactions, understanding domestic perceptions in China and travelling back to Delhi,” Mr. Misri said.

"Travel was extremely difficult. Anytime you flew out of China during COVID, returning meant a mandatory 21-day quarantine, 21 days of 'vanvaas' every time you visited Delhi for a day," the Foreign Secretary said.
“There was shock all around, even on the Chinese side, recognising that something very serious had happened,” he added.
"COVID had already created a lot of stress multilaterally, internationally, but also bilaterally because the Chinese felt they were being stigmatised and were being blamed for COVID-19," he said.
India never pointed fingers at China for the pandemic, Mr. Misri said. China, however, felt that the international community was determined to paint it black, he stated.

"So they had a very harsh response and harsh attitude to the international community in general for a while," he said, adding that it was also the reason for the "draconian lockdown" that China imposed on its citizens for a considerable time.

articles.title: Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul on his memoir ‘Without Fear or Favour ‘and the executive’s growing influence over the collegium system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former Supreme Court judge on delays in clearing collegium recommendations and the need for reform

Few judges have offered as candid an account of the inner workings of India’s higher judiciary as former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul. In his memoir, Without Fear or Favour (Juggernaut), he reflects on a judicial career spanning over two decades, offering a ringside view of the politics surrounding judicial appointments, the executive’s growing influence over the collegium system, and the quiet power struggles simmering beneath the judiciary’s institutional facade.

The memoir also offers a rare glimpse into the deliberations preceding some of the apex court’s most consequential judgments in recent years and the dilemmas confronting judges when called upon to reconcile competing interests. In an interview at his residence in New Delhi, the veteran jurist reflects on the need for systemic reforms and the challenges of preserving judicial independence.

articles.title: President Murmu inaugurates Simhastha Kumbh preparations in Nashik
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Along with President Droupadi Murmu, the ceremony was attended by Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Ajit Pawar, among other ministers of the State

President Droupadi Murmu conducted the flag worship ceremony of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela at the Kushavart Teerth in Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, on Saturday (October 31, 2026). While addressing the gathering at the Maha Goda Aarti ceremony, President Murmu called upon the people of India to make the upcoming Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela an example of social unity, environmental protection, cultural heritage preservation of India and integration of modern infrastructure with age-old religious rituals.
President said that the Kumbh was not only an event of religious faith but also provided an opportunity to bring about social harmony and positive transformation in India.

Talking about the drought situation in the State, President Murmu assured the farmers that the Centre and the Government of Maharashtra would extend the required assistance to them without undermining their dignity and self-respect. She said the government would always support the farmers, calling them the provider of the country’s food security.
Kumbh will transform Nashik and Trimbakeshwar; Says Fadnavis
Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said that the Kumbh reflected the confluence of the multiple expressions and traditions of ancient Indian Sanatan culture.
He called the gathering an event of faith not only for Indians but also for the devotees across the world, continuing the ancient tradition of a holy dip in the Ganga and Godavari.

He assured the gathering that the Government of Maharashtra was committed to making the upcoming Simhastha Kumbh a memorable one and transform the entire development scenario of Nashik and Trimbakeshwar.
Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, informed that the State Government is all set to welcome approximately 12 crore pilgrims from around the globe for the forthcoming Simhastha Kumbh.

According to him, about ₹35,000 crore worth of development projects are being implemented in Nashik-Trimbakeshwar area, and these developmental activities will not only be limited to Kumbh but will also bring in development thrust to the region in the long run.
He further added that the event must create employment opportunities for the people of the region and contribute to the economy of the region too.

articles.title: Taiwan says China harassing shipping with east coast patrol
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's "attempts to harass ships at sea through radio ‌communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality"

China's Coast Guard is harassing shipping with its latest patrol off Taiwan's east coast and trying ​to exert a fictional jurisdiction, the Taiwanese Coast Guard said, adding ‌it had sent its own ships to keep watch.

China, ​which views Taiwan as its own territory, ⁠has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty ‌claims, say they believe China is practising for a potential maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and ‌civilian assets.
Taipei regards the area off its east ‌coast ⁠as critical to wartime supply routes from allies ⁠in the event of a blockade or conflict. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan.

Responding late on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to China's announcement of its latest ​east coast patrol, Taiwan's ‌Coast Guard said two Chinese ships were involved and it had sent its own forces to monitor.
Chinese state media showed video of one of its ships broadcasting a ‌radio message that it was carrying out law enforcement ​and offering help should any be needed.
It did not say who the message was ⁠broadcast at, but showed footage of an unidentified fishing trawler.

Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's "attempts to harass ships at sea through radio ‌communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality".
"Our country holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan, and China has absolutely no jurisdiction over any of Taiwan's waters," it added.

China on ‌Saturday (October 31, 2026) also sent another Coast Guard ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas ​Islands, which are strategically located at the top of the South China Sea, Taiwan's Coast Guard said ⁠separately.
Taiwan has so far this year "expelled" Chinese Coast Guard vessels from ⁠Pratas waters 13 times, it added.

articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

With a smirk, Flávio Bolsonaro squinted at the camera and called President Lula da Silva “nine fingers” in the televised debate just two days before Brazil went to the polls for the presidential runoff. It was a cynical attempt to weaponise an old scar – and a gossip – against the Workers Party’s leader. Lula reacted sharply, reminding the audience how he had lost a finger on his left hand while working in a factory. “If there is anyone who lost a finger at the age of 17, it was me, working at night because I had to work,” Lula said, staring into the cameras. A red-faced Flavio didn’t know where to look. On October 25, Lula made history by becoming the first Brazilian president to finish second in the first round of an election, held on October 4, and go on to win the presidency in the run-off.

Ever since Lula entered politics more than three decades ago, his opponents have peddled the rumour that he deliberately chopped off his own finger to gain sympathy and claim compensation. But those familiar with his life know the struggles that shaped him. Born on October 27, 1945, in a dusty corner of Brazil, Lula grew up amid hunger and deprivation in the state of Pernambuco.

articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress
Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.
Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections

Congressman Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. He has criticised President Donald Trump’s policies as “utterly destructive”, described him as a “lame duck”, and said Democrats would prevail in the 2026 midterm elections and the 2028 presidential election.

Congresswoman Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, is seeking another term from Washington’s 7th Congressional District. In 2020, she became the second Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Ms. Jayapal traces her roots to Kerala. Her mother, Maya Jayapal, is a writer and counsellor and the author of Bangalore: Roots and Beyond .

Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress

Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.

Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections

Congressman Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. He has criticised President Donald Trump’s policies as “utterly destructive”, described him as a “lame duck”, and said Democrats would prevail in the 2026 midterm elections and the 2028 presidential election.

Congresswoman Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, is seeking another term from Washington’s 7th Congressional District. In 2020, she became the second Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.

Ms. Jayapal traces her roots to Kerala. Her mother, Maya Jayapal, is a writer and counsellor and the author of Bangalore: Roots and Beyond .

articles.title: Andhra civic polls: TDP, YSRCP workers clash in Pulivendula; slow turnout in cities | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fourteen vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula, Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh hours before polling began on Sunday

About 21.40 lakh of Andhra Pradesh’s 96.89 lakh urban voters had cast their votes by 11 a.m. on Sunday, a turnout of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission. Smaller towns are well ahead of cities. Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district leads the State at 60.92%, followed by Kuppam at 44.30% and Nagari at 40.46%. In Pulivendula, the scene of clashes this morning, 35.17% had voted.

The 13 municipal corporations are trailing: Chittoor leads them at 32.50%. Vijayawada was at 18.07% and Guntur at 17.82%. Visakhapatnam, the largest, was the lowest at 13.34%. 11 AM- Poll Percentage.pdf

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy is on a visit to Pulivendula in Kadapa district on Sunday, where municipal polling is under way. The TDP has accused him of taking part in a roadshow in alleged violation of the Model Code of Conduct.

Polling picked up in Visakhapatnam through the morning. Turnout rose from 3.34% at 9 a.m. to 13.34% by 11 a.m. on Sunday, according to election officials. Of the city’s 18.37 lakh voters, 2,45,251 had voted by then.

Only 3.34% of Visakhapatnam’s voters had cast their votes by 9 a.m. on Sunday, the lowest among the State’s 13 corporations. Of 18.38 lakh voters, 61,309 had voted. Madhurawada zone recorded the highest turnout at 5.87%, followed by Anakapalli at 5.18%. The South Assembly constituency was the lowest at 1.81%.
Vizag GVMC elections open with 3.34% turnout in first two hours; urban areas slower, with police security and active voter mobilization underway.
Stones were thrown in wards 11 and 12 of Pulivendula on Sunday. TDP and YSRCP workers pushed and jostled each other in several other wards.
The police chased away the fighting groups in places such as Islampuram. YSRCP workers accused the police of driving away their voters.

Voters had started queuing at 7 a.m. Hours earlier, around midnight, three cars, 10 motorcycles and a tractor were set on fire near an orchard belonging to one Madhusudhan Reddy. The police said it was not yet known who was behind it.
Several vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula town, few hours before the municipal elections began on Saturday (November 1) morning.

articles.title: Woman with disability dies in midnight fire at Korattur apartment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: An air-conditioner and a refrigerator, among other electrical appliances, reportedly exploded as the fire spread rapidly through the house. A suspected electrical short circuit is believed to have triggered the blaze

A 48-year-old woman with a disability died after being trapped in a fire that broke out at her apartment in Periyar Nagar, Korattur, in the early hours of Sunday (November 1, 2026). Her husband and son escaped with burn injuries.
The deceased has been identified as Akila, 48. Police said the incident occurred while the family of three was asleep.

An air-conditioner and a refrigerator, among other electrical appliances, reportedly exploded as the fire spread rapidly through the house. A suspected electrical short circuit is believed to have triggered the blaze.

The woman’s husband, Ramani, 55, and their son, Karthik, 25, managed to escape from the house despite suffering burn injuries. However, Akhila, who had a disability, could not get out and was trapped inside. She died in the fire.

On receiving information, personnel from the Korattur police and Fire and Rescue Services rushed to the spot and launched rescue operations with the help of local residents. Ramani and Karthik were rescued and taken to a hospital for treatment.
The Rajamangalam Police have launched an investigation into the incident.

fullParagraphs: Move reflects the closure of institutional avenues, says LoP Rahul Gandhi; terms it a political weapon against all who colluded to destroy votes; warns ECI officials that they are first target; says CEC should be tried for treason

The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) carried out a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, unanimously adopting a motion by a show of hands.

They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi described the exercise as a “political weapon” aimed at all those who had “colluded” to destroy the votes of the Indian people. He asserted that Mr. Kumar should not only be removed from office but also tried in a court of law for treason.

The Opposition was compelled to hold a public impeachment because “every other institution and institutional direction” was closed to it, Mr. Gandhi said in his concluding remarks, warning that those involved in alleged electoral irregularities “would not escape accountability and would eventually have to face the representatives of the people”.

The motion was initiated by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, whose official residence at 10, Rajaji Marg, served as the venue for the proceedings. Moving the motion, Mr. Kharge levelled six charges against the CEC, alleging that he had worked under the directions of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.

The proceedings, which continued for three-and-a-half hours, were modelled on those of Parliament, replicating the setting of the Lok Sabha, with former Speaker Meira Kumar presiding over the session.

Senior INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, occupied the front-row seats. Apart from Opposition MPs, civil society representatives, student leaders and voters who alleged that their names had been wrongfully deleted from electoral rolls during the SIR also took part in the proceedings.
Mr. Gandhi said the gathering in the garden of Mr. Kharge’s residence was unprecedented and reflected the closure of institutional avenues available to the Opposition.

“This may look like a meeting of MPs and ordinary citizens, but it is, in fact, a political weapon aimed directly at every single person who colluded to destroy the votes of the Indian people,” Mr. Gandhi said.

“You are hiding behind the institution you have sworn to protect. Remember, you cannot hide behind it forever. One day, you will have to face the representatives of the people of this country,” he added, addressing Mr. Kumar and other officials. He claimed that the CEC will not survive in his post once the Opposition brings out all the proofs into the public domain.

articles.title: Every squadron, air defence unit, air warrior must be ready to respond at moment’s notice: IAF Chief Dixit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Air Chief Marshal Dixit outlined his core focus areas under the acronym VAYU, defining his vision as Vigilance and operational readiness, Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance), Yukti (tactical innovation), and Unity of effort across the tri-services.

Newly-appointed Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said restoring the Indian Air Force's sanctioned fighter squadron strength, advancing self-reliance in terms of platforms and weapon systems and ensuring tri-services synergy will be his top priorities.

A day after assuming charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Dixit outlined his core focus areas under the acronym VAYU, defining his vision as Vigilance and operational readiness, Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance), Yukti (tactical innovation), and Unity of effort across the tri-services.

"Our security environment remains demanding. In addition, the character of war is being reshaped by new technologies and systems like drones, long-range precision weapons, space, cyber, AI and the electromagnetic spectrum," he said.
"The Air Force, while transforming into the force that India will need in the next decade, must always be ready to fight and win," he said.
Explaining the four pillars of his VAYU vision, the Chief of Air Staff said restoring the IAF's combat strength towards the sanctioned level will also be his "foremost task".
"V is for Vigilance and readiness. Every squadron, every radar, every air defence unit along with each and every air warrior must be ready to respond at a moment's notice," he stressed.
The IAF Chief, elaborating on Aatmanirbharta, said Indian sensors, platforms and weapons will be the force's highest priority.

"We will fight with Indian solutions, and we will hold them in numbers and that must sustain operations demands. Our responsibility is to fight and win, but most importantly it is to deter conflict through credible air power," he said.

"Y is for Yukti, our ingenuity. Innovation in doctrine, procedures and in technology: networked, AI-enabled command and control; layered counter-drone defence; responsive maintenance, force protection, resilience and use of near-space as operational domains for the Air Force, are all areas which will be constantly monitored and progressed," he said.

"In step with the vision of JAI, Jointness, Aatmanirbharta and Innovation, we will plan and fight as one along with our Army, our Navy and our national agencies. Air power delivers most when it is integrated from the very first plan," he noted.

Samajwadi Party workers gathered outside party chief Akhilesh Yadav's residence, while groups of Congress supporters assembled outside Himachal Bhawan before proceeding towards the rally venue.

Many supporters arrived in Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) morning, while several others had reached the national capital on Saturday (October 31, 2026) or earlier as parties mobilised their cadres from different states for the protest.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) urged people coming to Delhi for the protest to also shop from local traders ahead of Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj, asserting that the Opposition's programme would not hurt businesses.

articles.title: ‘Epstein Files’: U.S. Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper’s story was published in July 2025 detailing the President’s alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman

A U.S. Judge on Saturday (October 31, 2026) dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Mr. Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Mr. Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the President's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman.
Mr. Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal.

The report piled scrutiny on Mr. Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the President's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein.

In Saturday's (October 31, 2026) ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Mr. Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Mr. Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Mr. Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April.
The Judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Mr. Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice."
The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Mr. Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."
"We have certain things in common," says Mr. Trump, to which Epstein responds: "Yes, we do, come to think of it."
"Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" asks Mr. Trump.
"As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," says Epstein.

articles.title: Ra’am and Joint List | The surge of the other
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israel’s Arab parties made historic gains in elections but uncertainty remains whether the opposition bloc would join hands with them to form a government

On October 27, the day Israel went to the polls, the first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, the country recorded its highest voter turnout since 1999, at 77.7% But this was not the only story about the turnout.

Israel’s often overlooked Arab citizens, who make up some 20% of the population, made an overwhelming case for representation and change that day by turning out in massive numbers to vote. Exit polls recorded by Channel 12 estimated their turnout at nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade.

For the far-right coalition led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , the election was a “war for our home”, but for Arab parties, the political mobilisation meant meaningful representation in the Knesset , the Israeli parliament.

This mobilisation seems to have paid off. Arab parties have emerged as the third bloc after the elections. The Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am) have secured a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Parliament, their highest-ever tally.

Part of the credit goes to the Arab parties, which have actively mobilised their communities to vote. But much of it also goes to Mr. Netanyahu’s far-right government, whose policies and rhetoric, including the war on Gaza and escalating violence in the occupied West Bank, have heightened fears among Arab citizens.

While Arab citizens are affected like any other Israelis when it comes to national security, they’ve also borne the brunt of racism and violence. According to polls by the Israeli Democracy Institute, a party’s position related to crime in Arab society was one of the most important factors determining their vote.

Fear, as many experts have pointed out, has been their prime motivation, which Arab parties have been able to mobilise given the divisive campaigns launched by Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc. During the campaign, the Netanyahu camp put up billboards, saying it was ‘either the right or Palestine’. Even on the day of polling, the Prime Minister urged his supporters to go and vote, pointing to an Arab voter surge and calling it a matter of “life and death”.

While leaders of Arab parties have called Mr. Netanyahu’s attempts racist, they, too, have borne the brunt of discrimination. Like in the cases of previous elections, an attempt was made for disqualification of the Ra’am party and the Joint List (an alliance of Balad, Hadash and Ta’al) before the polls. The surge in voter turnout has helped them gain a significant number of seats, which would have made them kingmakers in a hung Parliament where no bloc has a clear majority. But neither side has expressed any willingness to form a government with Arab parties.

Mr. Netanyahu has accused the Arab parties of “stealing” the elections and has vowed to keep them out of power, while Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition coalition, has been reluctant to join hands with them.

This reluctance is not new. The Ra’am party, led by Mansour Abbas, became the first Arab party in nearly 44 years to be part of a government in 2021 when they backed the Bennett-Yair Lapid government. Ra’am broke off from the Joint List. However, this experiment was short-lived as the coalition collapsed within a year. Ra’am returned to the opposition fold after Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition won the elections in 2022.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 01 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Ra’am and Joint List | The surge of the other

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Israel’s Arab parties made historic gains in elections but uncertainty remains whether the opposition bloc would join hands with them to form a government

On October 27, the day Israel went to the polls, the first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, the country recorded its highest voter turnout since 1999, at 77.7% But this was not the only story about the turnout.

Israel’s often overlooked Arab citizens, who make up some 20% of the population, made an overwhelming case for representation and change that day by turning out in massive numbers to vote. Exit polls recorded by Channel 12 estimated their turnout at nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade.

For the far-right coalition led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , the election was a “war for our home”, but for Arab parties, the political mobilisation meant meaningful representation in the Knesset , the Israeli parliament.

This mobilisation seems to have paid off. Arab parties have emerged as the third bloc after the elections. The Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am) have secured a combined 19 seats in the 120-member Parliament, their highest-ever tally.

Part of the credit goes to the Arab parties, which have actively mobilised their communities to vote. But much of it also goes to Mr. Netanyahu’s far-right government, whose policies and rhetoric, including the war on Gaza and escalating violence in the occupied West Bank, have heightened fears among Arab citizens.

While Arab citizens are affected like any other Israelis when it comes to national security, they’ve also borne the brunt of racism and violence. According to polls by the Israeli Democracy Institute, a party’s position related to crime in Arab society was one of the most important factors determining their vote.

Fear, as many experts have pointed out, has been their prime motivation, which Arab parties have been able to mobilise given the divisive campaigns launched by Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc. During the campaign, the Netanyahu camp put up billboards, saying it was ‘either the right or Palestine’. Even on the day of polling, the Prime Minister urged his supporters to go and vote, pointing to an Arab voter surge and calling it a matter of “life and death”.

While leaders of Arab parties have called Mr. Netanyahu’s attempts racist, they, too, have borne the brunt of discrimination. Like in the cases of previous elections, an attempt was made for disqualification of the Ra’am party and the Joint List (an alliance of Balad, Hadash and Ta’al) before the polls. The surge in voter turnout has helped them gain a significant number of seats, which would have made them kingmakers in a hung Parliament where no bloc has a clear majority. But neither side has expressed any willingness to form a government with Arab parties.

Mr. Netanyahu has accused the Arab parties of “stealing” the elections and has vowed to keep them out of power, while Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the opposition coalition, has been reluctant to join hands with them.

This reluctance is not new. The Ra’am party, led by Mansour Abbas, became the first Arab party in nearly 44 years to be part of a government in 2021 when they backed the Bennett-Yair Lapid government. Ra’am broke off from the Joint List. However, this experiment was short-lived as the coalition collapsed within a year. Ra’am returned to the opposition fold after Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition won the elections in 2022.

Ra’am broke off from the Joint List. However, this experiment was short-lived as the coalition collapsed within a year. fullParagraphs: An experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 is a remarkable development because, instead of targeting the virus directly, it silences the viral DNA; this is promising because current treatments rarely eliminate the DNA, which allows the virus to rebound
In 1904, two scientists, Henry Wheeler and Treat Johnson, synthesised a variant of cytosine, one of the building blocks of DNA, in the laboratory.

The variant they synthesised contained a chemical tag called a methyl group (-CH 3 ) attached to cytosine, so they called it 5-methylcytosine. Their motivation for doing so was based on the observation that two other building blocks of DNA and its chemical cousin RNA, called thymine and uracil, differed only by the presence of a methyl group.

fullParagraphs: Fourteen vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula, Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh hours before polling began on Sunday

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy staged a sit-in outside the Returning Officer’s office in Pulivendula on Sunday, demanding a repoll in the town.He alleged that YSRCP polling agents had been denied entry into several polling booths. He had gone to the office to raise the issue with the Returning Officer, but officials reportedly did not let him in. He then sat down outside in protest.

Jaya Kumar, 66, a senior citizen with ailments, made his way to the polling station at Chepala Thimmapuram, Ward 5, in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, leaning on a bamboo stick for support. The ramp, the usual access route for those unable to take the stairs, was packed with voters standing in the queue behind its handrails. Mr. Jaya Kumar was told by the staff on duty to walk around the building and use the stairs at the other end. The queue continued well past noon.

Andhra Pradesh’s overall turnout in the urban local body elections rose to 37.13% by 1 p.m. on Sunday, up from 22.08% at 11 a.m., according to the State Election Commission. About 35.97 lakh of the 96.89 lakh voters had cast their votes.

Kanigiri in Markapuram district recorded the highest turnout, 63.36%, though only two of its wards are voting. Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district, voting in all 32 wards, was close behind at 61.86%, followed by Nagari at 60.81%. Pulivendula, the scene of this morning’s clashes , 51.51% had voted.

Among the 13 corporations, Machilipatnam is well ahead at 47.85%. Vijayawada was at 36.40% and Guntur at 30.94%. Visakhapatnam, which had the second-lowest turnout at 11 a.m., is now the lowest of all the urban bodies at 27.55%. 1 pm - Poll Percentage.pdf

State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and Secretary A. Mallikarjuna reviewed polling across the State through webcasting on Sunday. Some 13,500 CCTV cameras have been installed at polling stations, following the Supreme Court’s directions.

Medical staff and voters attend to Pasupuleti Narasimha Rao, 70, who collapsed while arriving to vote at the Ramanagar Municipal School polling station in Ongole on Sunday. He was taken to a hospital. Photo: Kommuri Srinivas Collapsed.jpeg

The YSRCP “seems to have come ‘well-prepared’ in Kadapa” while the rest of the State is voting peacefully, Minister Nara Lokesh said in a post on X on Sunday. The election authorities would deal with “criminal elements”, he said, urging voters to turn out in large numbers.

Turnout in Kadapa district’s urban bodies stood at 25.46% by 11 a.m., above the State average of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission’s figures. Jammalamadugu recorded 60.92% and Pulivendula 35.17%. Kadapa city, the district’s only corporation, was at 18.54%.

articles.title: Uttarakhand chopper crash: Mortal remains of all six victims recovered, sent to Rishikesh AIIMS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter

The mortal remains of all six people who died in the helicopter crash near Joshimath in Uttarakhand were recovered and sent to AIIMS, Rishikesh, on Sunday (November 1, 2026) morning, the Chamoli district administration said.
On Friday (October 30), the chopper crashed on a hillside near Chai village in Joshimath while it was returning to Dehradun from the Badrinath shrine.

The mortal remains were brought to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Joshimath, by road. Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter.

The district administration said that teams of the Indian Army, ITBP, SDRF, NDRF, police, district administration and the Forest Department jointly conducted the search operation amidst challenging conditions in the inaccessible and high-altitude hilly area.
"The bodies of all six deceased were taken out by rescue teams on foot on difficult mountain paths," mentions a statement issued by the district administration on Sunday (November 1).
The operation started on Friday (October 30) after the chopper crashed, but due to the difficult terrain and remote location, it took over 24 hours for teams to complete the operation.

articles.title: Mysuru City Corporation collects ₹210 crore in property tax so far this year: Yathindra Siddaramaiah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mysuru City Corporation had set a target of collecting ₹286.72 crore in property tax during 2026-27
Minister in charge of Mysuru district Yathindra Siddaramaiah said the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) has collected ₹210 crore in property tax so far during the current financial year.

He was delivering his Rajyothsava Day address in Mysuru on Sunday (November 1, 2026). It may be mentioned here that the MCC had set a target of collecting ₹286.72 crore in property tax during 2026-27.

During his address, Mr. Yathindra said a special ‘Prajaseva’ e-Khata campaign by charging a nominal fee of just ₹175 had been organised by MCC recently. During the campaign, over 590 property owners had been distributed e-khata documents within 72 hours of submitting their applications.
So far, around 78,000 ‘A’ and ‘B’ Khatas have been issued in MCC, he added.

GRAMANUBHAVA: Mr. Yathindra also launched the ‘Gramanubhava’ or Village Experience programme, an initiative by the State Government’s Department of School Education and Literacy aimed at creating awareness among urban students about rural life, agricultural culture, and their connection to the soil.
AWARDS: Meanwhile, a total of 92 persons were given away district level Rajyothsava awards on the occasion.
Also, SSLC and PUC students who studied in the Kannada medium at Government schools and secured the high marks were felicitated.

Narasimharaja Assembly constituency MLA Tanveer Sait, MLCs C.N. Manjegowda and Raghu, Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Zilla Panchayat CEO S. Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru City Police Commissioner Seema Latkar, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner M.K. Savitha, Additional Deputy Commissioner R. Aishwarya along with other officials, pro-Kannada activists, and dignitaries were present at the event.

articles.title: Foolish drama, will be final nail in coffin of Congress' political future: Nadda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Minister Nadda alleged that the protest was part of a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder

Union Minister J.P. Nadda on Sunday (November 1, 2026) slammed the Opposition INDIA bloc's rally as a "foolish and designed drama" and said it will prove to be the final "nail in the coffin" of Congress' "political downfall".
Mr. Nadda alleged that the protest was part of a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder.
INDIA block protest rally at Ramlila Maidan LIVE updates

In an apparent reference to the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, Mr. Nadda claimed that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's objective behind organising it on Sunday was to rub salt into the wounds of "Sikh brothers".

"Removing the democratically elected government by conspiring to spread riots and anarchy in Delhi, adversely impacting the earnings of shopkeepers and traders in Delhi during the festive season and defaming the country are other objectives of the rally," the senior BJP leader told reporters.

"The day of November 1 is the ugliest and darkest blot on India's democratic history. On this very day, goons patronised by Congress massacred our innocent Sikh brothers. Thousands and lakhs of Sikh families became homeless overnight."
Mr. Nadda said India is a strong democracy and will not be run by riot-based politics, but by the Constitution and the mandate of the people.
“Whatever is happening today at Ramlila Maidan is not respect for democracy, but a well-thought-out conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder.
"This is a foolish and designed drama of people who have been defeated and repeatedly rejected by the public. The public understands this very well,” he charged.

The Opposition alliance is holding the 'Chalo Dilli' protest in the national capital as part of its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

articles.title: GST mop-up grows 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh cr. in October
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

GST collections jumped 23% year-on-year to the second-highest level of over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October as festive buying boosted domestic demand, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, , 2026).
October is the second consecutive month when monthly gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and second only to the record about ₹2.43 lakh crore mop-up in April.
Also, the 22.9% year-on-year growth clocked during the month is the fastest recorded pace of gross mop-up in the current fiscal year.
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
In April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

Grant Thornton Bharat, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Manoj Mishra, said October collections capture the festive-season demand cycle, which typically brings higher consumer spending, retail activity and movement of goods across sectors.
The performance across key states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, also points to continued strength in GST collections across major economic centres.

The tourists had gone to the Dho area in Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality’s Ward No. 8, which was covered in heavy snow, according to Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Dhakal.

“We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon,” Ms. Dhakal told PTI .
The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, she said.

The guide contacted the District Administration Office in Dolpa on Saturday evening (October 31, 2026), saying the tourists might have been stranded due to heavy snowfall, she said. However, communication was completely disrupted on Sunday morning (November 1, 2026).
“We cannot say they are missing, as we have located the area,” Ms. Dhakal clarified.

The tourists have been identified as Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Bishwas and Rajesh De, according to a press release issued by the District Administration Office, Dolpa.
Security personnel are being mobilised, and a rescue helicopter is expected to arrive soon, the press release said.

articles.title: President Trump says U.S. still has ‘one or two targets’ in Iran
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The President said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear programme

President Donald Trump said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked.
Mr. Trump maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war, which was started by the United States and Israel in February, were “going fine but you know they’re not very reliable.”
The President said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear programme.
“We’ve knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Mr. Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.
“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.
The Iranian government denied any nuclear work is carried out there.

Earlier Saturday (October 31, 2026), U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Mr. Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran and that the United States would be open to a diplomatic solution.

Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday (October 31, 2026) warned the United States and Israel against launching a new offensive, following threats they could resume strikes after crucial elections in both countries.

Mr. Trump had previously warned an attack could come after the U.S. midterms this week, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke of a “historic, one-time opportunity” to topple the Iranian government.
The elections in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted in a general election on Tuesday but yet to form a new government.

fullParagraphs: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan, on Saturday, accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties

Pakistan has warned Afghanistan that it reserves the right to take all necessary measures to eliminate cross-border terror threats , asserting that terrorism remains a "red line" and its national security cannot be held hostage to the Taliban regime's "inaction".

In a strongly worded statement issued Saturday (October 31, 2026) night, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties.
The latest remarks by the Afghan Taliban spokesperson exposed the regime's “deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan”, it said.
"Pakistan’s position is unequivocal: Terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable,” the Ministry said.
The statement came in response to remarks made by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who accused Pakistan of being unwilling to resolve tensions with Afghanistan through dialogue.

In an interview to Hurriyat Radio on Saturday (October 31, 2026), the spokesperson said Islamabad lacked the necessary readiness for a peaceful resolution of differences and its “wrong policies” were preventing a resolution of the conflict.

The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations, which is its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, the statement said.

"The Taliban regime's persistent refusal to address terrorism remains the principal obstacle to normal relations. Shifting blame, making hollow assurances and questioning Pakistan’s policies will neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities,” it said.

articles.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Arab-majority parties made major gains in elections, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them

Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to urge the opposition to ally with Arab parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , who has gone on the offensive against the minority group's leaders.

Arab-majority parties made major gains in Tuesday’s election, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them.
Joining a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said that the Arab community, which accounts for around 20% of Israel's population, had a right to political participation.
"It's the last chance for real change," the 60-year-old psychologist said, warning that Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, was a "great manipulator".
"We need to give peace a chance," she said. "Otherwise we'll have this bloodshed forever."
Tuesday’s election was inconclusive, with neither bloc reaching a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.
Jewish-majority parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu, known by his nickname Bibi, won 48 seats, while two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.
An alliance between the two camps would potentially give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, but the idea is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.
"Arabs and Jews will only win together" and "There is a majority for change" read some of the signs held by around 500 protesters in Tel Aviv.
"67 — United we stand, divided we get Bibi" and "Why not, really — unless we are racist?" read some of the placards at the 100-strong rally in Jerusalem.
