articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 57 discusses mapping the human brain, potential of brain atlases and more
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The episode discusses a new technology developed at IIT Madras to create detailed three-dimensional maps of the human brain, the recently released C-STROKE atlas and plans to map more than 100 brains
The 57th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu explores how researchers are using advanced imaging and reconstruction techniques to create detailed, three-dimensional maps of the human brain.

Zubeda Hamid, senior assistant editor, The Hindu, speaks to Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam, Head of the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, about the technology, how the maps are created and what they could reveal about the human brain.

The episode looks at C-STROKE, a recently released three-dimensional atlas of a stroke-affected brain. Unlike conventional MRI scans, which provide images of the brain at a particular resolution, the new approach allows researchers to examine brain structures in greater detail and build comprehensive 3D maps.

The discussion explains how researchers prepare brain tissue, use imaging techniques and reconstruct the data to create these maps. It also looks at the different scientific and technological disciplines involved in the process and how detailed mapping could help researchers study the brain’s structure and changes associated with neurological conditions.

Another focus is the Centre’s plan to map more than 100 human brains across different stages of life. The project aims to build a larger collection of brain maps that could help researchers understand variations in brain structure, study neurological conditions and expand the available resources for brain research.

The episode also examines the potential applications of these atlases in clinical research and healthcare, including how they could contribute to a better understanding of stroke and other brain conditions. It discusses the possibilities as well as the work needed before such maps can be translated into clinical applications.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Polling ends peacefully across Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Municipal elections in Guntur, Bapatla and Palnadu districts concluded largely peacefully on Sunday. Election authorities said some complaints were received in Palnadu and Bapatla districts, but the issues were promptly addressed. District Collectors inspected polling stations and reviewed arrangements to ensure smooth voting.

In Guntur district, the Guntur Municipal Corporation (GMC), with 76 wards, 596 polling booths and 6,18,714 voters, recorded 3,18,009 votes, a turnout of 51.40%, by 5 p.m. Tenali Municipality, comprising 52 wards and 185 polling stations, registered 88,764 votes from 1,57,089 voters, recording 56.51%.

District Collector and District Election Officer C.M. Saikanth Varma inspected polling arrangements in Guntur. He directed officials to assist voters through help desks and prioritise senior citizens, pregnant women, nursing mothers and those who were unwell. He also instructed staff to arrange tricycles for persons with disabilities when required.

In Bapatla district, Repalle Municipality recorded 25,776 votes from 37,008 voters across 44 polling stations, registering 69.65% turnout by 5 p.m. Chirala, with 88 polling stations and 69,557 voters, recorded 50,558 votes, or 72.69%. These included 24,247 male and 26,311 female voters. Bapatla District Collector Vinod Kumar V. said complaints received during polling were attended immediately and the elections concluded peacefully.

Palnadu district recorded its highest turnout in Sattenapalli at 76.17%, with 36,712 votes polled from 48,196 voters across 36 wards. Vinukonda, also with 36 wards, recorded 35,012 votes from 47,186 voters, a turnout of 74.20%. Macherla registered 31,145 votes from 46,520 voters, or 66.95%, across 36 wards. Chilakaluripeta, with 48 wards and 86,554 voters, recorded 56,606 votes, translating to 65.40%.

Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla inspected polling stations in Macherla and said polling was peaceful across the district, with good voter participation and essential facilities provided. She said webcasting was arranged at every polling station, while strong rooms were secured with CCTV cameras. Contesting candidates were also permitted to inspect strong rooms to address their concerns, ensuring transparency in the electoral process.

articles.title: Electric fence defunct in Puzhal prison for the past 3 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Steps taken to restore live power using alternating current supply

The solar-powered electric fence along the perimeter wall of the Puzhal prison complex, one of the largest prisons in the country, has remained defunct for three years, official sources said on Sunday.

With no contract for annual maintenance, the solar-powered fence failed about three years ago. When a Nepal national inmate scaled the perimeter wall and escaped from the prison recently and later captured, it was reported the power supply in the fence was not functional due to rains.

However, the sources said the electric fence had no power supply for a long time. Confirming this to ‘The Hindu’, a senior official in the prison department said steps had been taken to restore power using Alternating Current (AC) like in other central prisons.

The Puzhal prison complex built on a sprawling 212 acres of land houses the Central Prison-I (Convicts), Central Prison-II (Remand Prisoners) and Special Prison for Women. The complex built by the Tamil Nadu Police Housing Corporation was inaugurated by the then Chief Minister in 2006.
In a related development, the Tamil Nadu Prison Department has suspended out-gang duties preventing convicts from going out for managing fuel stations, prison bazaar stores etc.

Additional Director-General of Police, Prisons, K. Shankar said the decision was taken as a precautionary measure. About 100 convicts were deployed in fuel stations located close to 11 central prisons across Tamil Nadu and other small business establishments like ‘Freedom Bazaar’ that sell products manufactured by inmates in the prison industry.

“There are chances that they (the convicts on out-gang duties) might escape. The decision to suspend the deployment of convicts on duties outside the prison is a temporary measure. The fuel stations will continue to be operated by the Indian Oil Corporation,” the ADGP said.

Mr. Shankar took charge as the ADGP, Prisons, a couple of days ago after DGP Sandeep Rai Rathore was transferred following the sensational jailbreak in Theni where 17 inmates escaped from the district jail after overpowering the prison warders on duty. All the escapees were recaptured by the Tamil Nadu police who launched a massive combing operation and also flew drones over forest areas abutting Theni and neighbouring Keralam.

articles.title: Tirupati municipal elections see low voter turnout

fullParagraphs: Tirupati registered the lowest poll share at 45.26%, while the district averaged 53.65%
The elections to the urban local bodies in Tirupati district concluded in a peaceful manner, with the poll percentage reportedly reflecting an urban apathy.

At 45.26 per cent, Tirupati registered the lowest poll percentage in the entire district, till about 5 p.m. With half a dozen universities, institutes such as IIT and IISER, and prominent industries, the city is known for its elite, educated and responsible citizen population comprising academicians, retired bureaucrats and technocrats.

However, the urban indifference was quite conspicuous in the polls held for the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC), as evident from the abysmal figure. Of the 2,90,492 total voters, only 1,31,476 showed up at the polling stations to cast their vote.

District Collector S. Venkateswar, along with District Revenue Officer G. Narasimhulu, monitored the developments at the various polling stations through webcasting.

The Election Expenditure Observer Mahaboob Basha visited several polling stations in Venkatagiri, Sullurpeta and Naidupeta municipalities and instructed the officials to adhere to the guidelines pertaining to monitoring the expenditure.

articles.title: Oocyte extraction racket: Women paid ₹20,000 as operators made around ₹3 lakh per cycle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police probe alleged exploitation of 43 women, including possible forged consent documents and illegal commissions, while examining recruitment networks, payment trails and the role of IVF and fertility centres in Hyderabad

Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.

The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.

The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.

The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.

Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Rajyotsava celebrated in Raichur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister recalls the century-long struggle to bring Kannada-speaking regions under a unified State

​Minister for Minor Irrigation, Science and Technology and Raichur district in-charge Ajay Singh praised the immense contribution made by leaders and freedom fighters who spearheaded the Karnataka unification movement, highlighting the State’s rich cultural heritage and religious tolerance.

​Addressing a gathering after unfurling the national flag during the 71st Kannada Rajyotsava celebrations at the Mahatma Gandhi District Stadium in Raichur on Sunday, Dr. Singh recalled the century-long struggle to bring Kannada-speaking regions under a unified State as they lay scattered under the British administration.

​”Deputy Chennabasappa initiated the movement for unification as early as 1856. The century-long agitation culminated in the creation of the unified Mysore State on November 1, 1956, which was subsequently renamed Karnataka by the then Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs on November 1, 1973,” Dr. Singh said.

​He remembered the invaluable contribution of prominent stalwarts, including Alur Venkataraya (Kannada Kulapurohita), Acharya B.M. Srikanthaiah, A.N. Krishnarao, Hardekar Manjappa, Kuvempu, S. Nijalingappa, H.S. Doreswamy, Bellary Siddamma and Patil Puttappa, among others.
​Highlighting the State’s literary and cultural achievements, the Minister noted that Karnataka remains a sanctuary of religious tolerance, moral conduct and peaceful coexistence.
He added that it is a matter of immense pride that Kannada literature has been honoured with eight Jnanpith awards.

​Explaining about the administrative and developmental measures, Dr. Singh stated that the State government has responded effectively to the severe drought situation, declaring 226 taluks State-wide, including all taluks in Raichur district, as drought affected.

​He noted that Raichur district faced a 49% rainfall deficit receiving only 222.5 mm of rainfall during the monsoon season (June to September) against the normal average of 439.6 mm. Deficits across individual taluks ranged between 35% and 62%.
​Under the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB), an action plan involving 890 development works worth ₹622.35 crore has been approved for Raichur district for 2025-26.
Out of these, 61 works have been completed, 394 are in progress, while an expenditure of ₹178.03 crore has been incurred so far.

Minister recalls the century-long struggle to bring Kannada-speaking regions under a unified State

​Minister for Minor Irrigation, Science and Technology and Raichur district in-charge Ajay Singh praised the immense contribution made by leaders and freedom fighters who spearheaded the Karnataka unification movement, highlighting the State’s rich cultural heritage and religious tolerance.

​Addressing a gathering after unfurling the national flag during the 71st Kannada Rajyotsava celebrations at the Mahatma Gandhi District Stadium in Raichur on Sunday, Dr. Singh recalled the century-long struggle to bring Kannada-speaking regions under a unified State as they lay scattered under the British administration.

​”Deputy Chennabasappa initiated the movement for unification as early as 1856. The century-long agitation culminated in the creation of the unified Mysore State on November 1, 1956, which was subsequently renamed Karnataka by the then Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs on November 1, 1973,” Dr. Singh said.

​He remembered the invaluable contribution of prominent stalwarts, including Alur Venkataraya (Kannada Kulapurohita), Acharya B.M. Srikanthaiah, A.N. Krishnarao, Hardekar Manjappa, Kuvempu, S. Nijalingappa, H.S. Doreswamy, Bellary Siddamma and Patil Puttappa, among others.

​Highlighting the State’s literary and cultural achievements, the Minister noted that Karnataka remains a sanctuary of religious tolerance, moral conduct and peaceful coexistence.

He added that it is a matter of immense pride that Kannada literature has been honoured with eight Jnanpith awards.

​Explaining about the administrative and developmental measures, Dr. Singh stated that the State government has responded effectively to the severe drought situation, declaring 226 taluks State-wide, including all taluks in Raichur district, as drought affected.

​He noted that Raichur district faced a 49% rainfall deficit receiving only 222.5 mm of rainfall during the monsoon season (June to September) against the normal average of 439.6 mm. Deficits across individual taluks ranged between 35% and 62%.

​Under the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB), an action plan involving 890 development works worth ₹622.35 crore has been approved for Raichur district for 2025-26.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Heavy snowfall and adverse conditions affect operations; SDRF resorts to aerial reconnaissance through a helicopter

The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) initiated a search and rescue operation on Sunday for seven trekkers and one guide who went missing after being stranded on the Kedartal trek in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand .

On October 27, a group of 13 people, consisting of seven trekkers and six support staff, set out from Gangotri for the Kedartal trek. They were scheduled to return on October 29, but adverse weather conditions, including glaciers and snowfall, blocked their route and prevented their timely return.

A team from Gangotri had already reached the Kedartal area for an initial assessment. However, heavy snowfall and adverse conditions hindered their progress. As a result, the SDRF has decided to conduct aerial reconnaissance and search the region using a helicopter.
Officials said that under the directives of SDRF Commandant Arpan Yaduvanshi, a specialised mountaineering team had been deployed to locate the missing individuals.

Two SDRF personnel, head constable Ravi Chauhan and constable Deepak Pant, reached Harsil by helicopter on Sunday, from where they conducted two thorough aerial reconnaissance flights over the Kedartal area. No clear signs of the missing trekkers or their tents were spotted during these flights, officials said.

Another team from the SDRF battalion headquarters has been sent out, equipped with essential rescue and mountaineering gear, to ensure that the search and rescue operation can continue as soon as conditions improve.

articles.title: India’s coal imports decline 5.83% in August
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: According to a statement from the Coal Ministry, the decline was primarily led by the power sector whose imports during the reported period declined 6.4% overall.

India’s overall import of coal fell 5.83% in August from the same period last year on the back of increased domestic production of the fossil fuel compound and reduced their shipments from overseas, according to government data.
The country imported 104.57 million tonnes (MT) of coal in August, compared to 111.05 MT in the same period last year.
Imports by domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants, that require the carbon-based compound for blending purposes, slumped 35.23% to 3 MT.
However, imports of thermal power plants that run solely on imported coal registered an uptick of about 1% at 18.31 MT.
Overall, coal imports by the power sector slumped about 6.4%.
The share of imported coal in India’s overall consumption basket declined to 19.3% in August this year compared to 21.2% in the same month last year.
Other than the power sector, coking coal, which serves as an important input for the steel industry, also declined about 4.2% during the reported period to 27.3 MT.
India depends on imports to meet 95% of its coking coal requirements. Import requirements are therefore subject to the demand of the steel sector.

Reflecting on the import dynamics, the Union Coal Ministry held, “The decline in overall coal imports, particularly imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants, underscores the importance of strengthening domestic production, transportation and supply-chain infrastructure,” adding that imports by imported coal-based power plants and the steel sector reflect their specific fuel and raw material requirements.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Frankfurt became the hot spot for ⁠violent protests after tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets of dozens of German cities during the day to demand better education ‌and lower living costs

German ministers threatened tough penalties for looters and rioters ​who damaged stores and injured more than 100 police officers in ‌Frankfurt overnight, still praising public forces for preventing larger-scale violence.

Frankfurt ​late on Saturday (October 31, 2026) became the hot spot for ⁠violent protests after tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets of dozens of German cities during the day to demand better education ‌and lower living costs in protests led by the campaign group “Gen Z regelt” — “Gen Z takes charge”.

In the ‌financial hub Frankfurt, hooded rioters damaged 17 shops and ‌stores, ⁠of which five were looted, Roman Poseck, interior minister ⁠of the state of Hesse, told a press conference on Sunday (November 1).
He said police deployed 1,300 officers, with more than 100 injured in clashes. Police arrested ​54 people aged between ‌13 and 29.
“I am shocked by what I have seen, and there is no point in sugar-coating it. Let me make this very clear: Things cannot go on like this,” ‌Mr. Poseck said.
Mr. Poseck said most of those arrested were ​German nationals, adding that many of those involved in the disturbances were of a migrant background, citing information ⁠from the police.
“Police currently estimate that they are dealing with between 1,000 and 1,500 violent troublemakers, predominantly from a migrant background,” ‌he added.
Frankfurt police reported violent disturbances including windows being smashed and petrol bombs being thrown at the emergency services.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt was quoted as telling the Bild tabloid on Sunday (November 1), “The rioters and looters will be identified and held accountable. This breach of the peace must be followed by tough penalties.”
He ‌accused “violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from the migrant community” of hijacking the ​otherwise peaceful protests, without elaborating.

articles.title: Somali pirates seize Iranian fishing vessel, raising fears of attacks on cargo ships
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Azini was hijacked on October 29 between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said

Somali pirates have seized an Iranian fishing vessel carrying 23 people, the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean said, warning that the ship was approaching a commercial shipping lane and could become a floating base for further attacks.

The Azini was hijacked on Thursday (October 29, 2026) between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The officer told The Associated Press that 12 pirates seized the vessel, which was carrying 21 Iranian crew members and two Somali security guards. He spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorised to speak with the media.

The crew's safety was unknown, the centre said in an alert dated on Saturday (October 31, 2026). In an updated warning, it said that pirates could use the vessel as a “mother ship” to support attacks on commercial vessels.
The European Union's naval Operation Atalanta was investigating. The centre urged ships in the area to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity.

The seizure follows a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. By August, pirates had hijacked six commercial vessels since April, with some attacks taking place far from Somalia's coastline. The captures included the oil products tanker Sibu 1, seized about 136 nautical miles (252 kilometres) east of al-Mukalla, Yemen.

In September, Puntland authorities said pirates killed five crew members of the tanker MT Honour 25 before security forces recovered the vessel. The tanker had been held since April. Authorities said that 16 suspected pirates were detained.

The renewed piracy adds another danger for shipping in a region already disrupted by the Iran war. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels against Saudi-linked shipping through Bab el-Mandeb have complicated routes used to move oil to world markets.

Those disruptions have lengthened voyages and driven up tanker costs. The AP reported in September that some oil shipments diverted around Africa faced journeys up to a month longer, while daily spot charter rates for tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz had reached $1 million.

International naval patrols and improved maritime security sharply reduced Somali piracy over the past decade. The latest seizures have renewed concerns about the threat to vessels off the country's long coastline.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

The Azini was hijacked on October 29 between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said

Somali pirates have seized an Iranian fishing vessel carrying 23 people, the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean said, warning that the ship was approaching a commercial shipping lane and could become a floating base for further attacks.

The Azini was hijacked on Thursday (October 29, 2026) between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The officer told The Associated Press that 12 pirates seized the vessel, which was carrying 21 Iranian crew members and two Somali security guards. He spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorised to speak with the media.

The crew's safety was unknown, the centre said in an alert dated on Saturday (October 31, 2026). In an updated warning, it said that pirates could use the vessel as a “mother ship” to support attacks on commercial vessels.

The European Union's naval Operation Atalanta was investigating. The centre urged ships in the area to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity.

The seizure follows a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. By August, pirates had hijacked six commercial vessels since April, with some attacks taking place far from Somalia's coastline. The captures included the oil products tanker Sibu 1, seized about 136 nautical miles (252 kilometres) east of al-Mukalla, Yemen.

In September, Puntland authorities said pirates killed five crew members of the tanker MT Honour 25 before security forces recovered the vessel. The tanker had been held since April. Authorities said that 16 suspected pirates were detained.

The renewed piracy adds another danger for shipping in a region already disrupted by the Iran war. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels against Saudi-linked shipping through Bab el-Mandeb have complicated routes used to move oil to world markets.

Those disruptions have lengthened voyages and driven up tanker costs. The AP reported in September that some oil shipments diverted around Africa faced journeys up to a month longer, while daily spot charter rates for tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz had reached $1 million.

International naval patrols and improved maritime security sharply reduced Somali piracy over the past decade. The latest seizures have renewed concerns about the threat to vessels off the country's long coastline.

articles.title: S. Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish, South Korean counterparts; discusses Ukraine, West Asia
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The External Affairs Minister also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held separate meetings with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts in the U.S., discussing the Ukraine conflict, the situation in West Asia, bilateral ties and multilateral issues.
The meetings took place on Saturday (October 31, 2026) on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta.
In a social media post, Mr. Jaishankar said he "discussed the Ukraine conflict, Gulf situation and multilateral issues" with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
The External Affairs Minister also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, with discussions focusing on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20.
Poland is attending this year's G20 meetings as a full participant following an invitation from the U.S. It has also expressed interest in securing permanent membership of the grouping.
“My meeting with DPM & FM Radosław Sikorski @sikorskiradek of Poland focused on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20,” Mr. Jaishankar said.
Mr. Jaishankar also met South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and discussed bilateral cooperation and other multilateral issues.
“Appreciated the stocktaking with @FMChoHyun of the Republic of Korea of our bilateral cooperation, as also the discussion on G20 and multilateral issues,” he said.

After two days of brainstorming on global affairs, Jaishankar and fellow G20 foreign ministers attended the college football game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

“Happy to introduce my fellow foreign ministers to the quintessential American sport of football and welcome them to #GatorNation,” Mr. Rubio posted on social media after escorting the visitors to the stands of the stadium.

articles.title: India's flight disruptions to Saudi Arabia continue amid security concerns
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The flight disruptions have continued amid attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including airports

Flight disruptions between India and Saudi Arabia continue, with Akasa Air on Sunday (November 1, 2026) extending the suspension of its services to Jeddah until November 18 amid the prevailing security situation in the Gulf kingdom. The airline said flights to and from Riyadh would remain suspended until November 30.
The announcement came two days after Air India and Air India Express said their flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh, and Dammam would remain suspended until November 14.
The flight disruptions have continued amid attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including airports.

In a statement on October 22, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said one Indian national was killed and two others injured in the October 21 attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Another Indian national was injured in an attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province.
The Embassy said it was in contact with Saudi authorities and would provide all possible assistance to the affected Indians.
Earlier, India had condemned attacks targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, saying the targeting of civilian infrastructure was unacceptable.

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for several attacks on Saudi targets, including airports and energy infrastructure. The group has carried out missile and drone attacks on the kingdom amid the wider regional conflict.

In its advisories, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh has asked Indian nationals to remain calm and vigilant, stay indoors in the event of an aerial attack and follow instructions issued by local authorities.
It also urged them not to circulate or repost videos or news related to the ongoing developments.

The Consulate General of India in Jeddah has been coordinating with airlines, local authorities, and community organisations to assist affected Indian nationals, particularly Umrah pilgrims, and facilitate alternative travel arrangements.

articles.title: Swimmer’s ear doesn’t just affect swimmers – two ear doctors explain what you need to know about this painful condition
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected
Many forms of ear infections strike children and adults alike, but among the most common is acute otitis externa , also known as swimmer’s ear.
About 10% of Americans will experience swimmer’s ear during their lifetimes . Adults are affected more commonly , and children only rarely, generally ages 5 to 12.

But you don’t have to be swimming to get swimmer’s ear. Go out jogging or walking, or do yardwork on a hot day, and moisture from perspiration can drip in your ear. However, the occurrence increases fivefold in swimmers – thus the reason the condition came to be called “swimmer’s ear.” It also occurs more frequently in tropical climates because of humidity and higher temperatures.

As doctors who specialise in ear problems, we are actively involved in research and clinical treatment for children and adults struggling with ear, nose and throat problems. Practicing in the state of Florida, we’ve certainly seen our share of patients with swimmer’s ear.

Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected. Moisture trapped in the canal leads to a break in the skin barrier and creates an opening for certain bacteria types to enter or existing ones to overgrow.

One of these culprits is the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is present in soil and water throughout the world. These bacteria favor moist areas, such as sinks, toilets, inadequately chlorinated swimming pools and hot tubs, as well as outdated or inactivated antiseptic solutions.

If you have the infection, you’ll know it. Symptoms generally appear a few days after infection. The main symptom of swimmer’s ear is severe pain and discomfort. It’s particularly noticeable when the outer ear is tugged, or by touching the tragus – that’s the small bump at the front of your ear. Other symptoms include itchiness inside the ear, redness, swelling and drainage. A feeling of fullness, or the perception of a plugged ear, may also occur, along with disturbed balance and temporary hearing loss.

Numerous factors can predispose someone to swimmer’s ear . They include a narrow ear canal, and skin diseases such as eczema or psoriasis. In addition, individuals wearing ear plugs, ear buds or hearing aids may be at an increased risk. Diabetics may also be more prone to the infection .
Swimmer’s ear can also come from something getting stuck inside the ear, excessive ear cleaning or contact with chemicals in hair dye or hairspray.

Swimmer’s ear is diagnosed after a health care provider has gathered a thorough history and examined the inside of the ear. The ear canal will typically look red, swollen and moist. There is also a possibility of fluid drainage or the appearance of scaly, shedding skin. Depending on the degree of swelling, the eardrum may be hard to see. A sample of fluid may be removed from the ear and sent to a lab to look for bacteria or fungus.

📰 Swimmer’s ear doesn’t just affect swimmers – two ear doctors explain what you need to know about this painful condition

Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected

Many forms of ear infections strike children and adults alike, but among the most common is acute otitis externa , also known as swimmer’s ear.

About 10% of Americans will experience swimmer’s ear during their lifetimes . Adults are affected more commonly , and children only rarely, generally ages 5 to 12.

But you don’t have to be swimming to get swimmer’s ear. Go out jogging or walking, or do yardwork on a hot day, and moisture from perspiration can drip in your ear. However, the occurrence increases fivefold in swimmers – thus the reason the condition came to be called “swimmer’s ear.” It also occurs more frequently in tropical climates because of humidity and higher temperatures.

As doctors who specialise in ear problems, we are actively involved in research and clinical treatment for children and adults struggling with ear, nose and throat problems. Practicing in the state of Florida, we’ve certainly seen our share of patients with swimmer’s ear.

Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected. Moisture trapped in the canal leads to a break in the skin barrier and creates an opening for certain bacteria types to enter or existing ones to overgrow.

One of these culprits is the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is present in soil and water throughout the world. These bacteria favor moist areas, such as sinks, toilets, inadequately chlorinated swimming pools and hot tubs, as well as outdated or inactivated antiseptic solutions.

If you have the infection, you’ll know it. Symptoms generally appear a few days after infection. The main symptom of swimmer’s ear is severe pain and discomfort. It’s particularly noticeable when the outer ear is tugged, or by touching the tragus – that’s the small bump at the front of your ear. Other symptoms include itchiness inside the ear, redness, swelling and drainage. A feeling of fullness, or the perception of a plugged ear, may also occur, along with disturbed balance and temporary hearing loss.

Numerous factors can predispose someone to swimmer’s ear . They include a narrow ear canal, and skin diseases such as eczema or psoriasis. In addition, individuals wearing ear plugs, ear buds or hearing aids may be at an increased risk. Diabetics may also be more prone to the infection .

Swimmer’s ear can also come from something getting stuck inside the ear, excessive ear cleaning or contact with chemicals in hair dye or hairspray.

Swimmer’s ear is diagnosed after a health care provider has gathered a thorough history and examined the inside of the ear. The ear canal will typically look red, swollen and moist. There is also a possibility of fluid drainage or the appearance of scaly, shedding skin. Depending on the degree of swelling, the eardrum may be hard to see. A sample of fluid may be removed from the ear and sent to a lab to look for bacteria or fungus.

Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting are among the most distressing side effects of cancer treatment in children. Preventing them is essential not only to improve quality of life, but also to help patients complete treatment. Yet the medicines used to prevent vomiting can themselves cause adverse effects, making the search for safe alternatives an important challenge in paediatric oncology.

articles.title: There’s new guidance on menopause symptoms like hot flashes. What women need to know
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come along with menopause
For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come with menopause.

Doctors stressed the importance of hormone therapies, which many women are considering again after the removal of federal safety warnings. On Friday, federal officials said the Food and Drug Administration has been taking steps to ensure there's an adequate supply.
Doctors also described various nonhormonal options in the new advice released this month by the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists, or ACOG.
“We would love our patients to go to their OB-GYNs regarding questions about menopause and really advocate for getting the treatment that they need,” said Camille Clare, the group’s president.

Menopause occurs when a woman has gone 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period. In the U.S., it usually happens around age 50. The time leading up to it is called perimenopause, during which the body’s production of the hormones estrogen and progesterone declines sharply.

Problems commonly arise. More than half of women in menopause report having “vasomotor” issues such as hot flashes and night sweats, said ACOG. As many as two-thirds report menopause-related sleep disruption. And more than a third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women worldwide report depressive symptoms.
In the past, doctors said, many women quietly suffered.

There's growing consensus that "these symptoms should be treated,” said JoAnn Manson, a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. “This should help to empower women to discuss their symptoms with their healthcare provider.”
Manson said ACOG’s new guidelines are similar to those put out by other medical organizations.

"Moderate to severe or bothersome menopausal symptoms should be treated with hormone therapy as the first line of treatment,” she said. While it's not appropriate for all women, she added, it’s a good option for many.

articles.title: West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: During his first visit to Thakurbari in North 24 Parganas after taking up the office of Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari says West Bengal would have turned into Bangladesh had the BJP not come to power in 2026

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said the State government had set a target of granting citizenship certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas in the State under the Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 by December 2026.

Mr. Adhikari, who visited the religious headquarters of Matuas at Thakurnagar, said only 25,000 people received citizenship under the CAA so far. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had promised granting citizenship to Matuas, largely described as Namashudras who had migrated from Bangladesh, under the CAA during the 2026 Assembly polls.

“We will expedite the hearing and provide citizenship to 2.5 lakh petitioners by December 31. Only 25,000 people have received citizenship under the CAA in West Bengal so far,” the Chief Minister said. Mr. Adhikari added that the State government would take initiative to include the name of those who receive CAA certificate into the voter list in the month of January when the process of enlisting new names in the voter list starts.

Earlier in August this year, Mr. Adhikari had said that out of 2.30 lakh applications filed under the CAA, 23,000 certificates had been issued. Earlier this year, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) transferred the processing of pending citizenship applications under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), 2019, from Empowered Committees to District Collectors in eight States and Union Territories including West Bengal.

During his first visit to Thakurbari in North 24 Parganas after taking up the office of Chief Minister, Mr. Adhikari said West Bengal would have turned into Bangladesh had the BJP not come to power in 2026. He thanked the Matuas for support in the 2026 Assembly polls and said the government in the State could not have been formed without the support of people from the Matua community. In the recently concluded Assembly polls, the BJP had won a majority of the Assembly seats in the Matua-dominated constituencies in North 24 Parganas and Nadia districts.

The Chief Minister promised to reconstitute the Matua Development Board and added that ₹50 crore would be spent for the development of the community through the board in the current financial year. The Chief Secretary had been instructed to ensure that there was no problem in getting SC certificates for Scheduled Caste communities who had CAA certificates.

The Chief Minister also blamed his predecessor for opposing the CAA. ”I am happy to be here. If I can do anything for Thakurnagar, that would be my biggest achievement. The previous Chief Minister had divided the Matuas and their society and did nothing for them. In fact, she directly opposed the CAA. In the coming days, I will work for them,” Mr. Adhikari said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Says Vigilance probe selectively targets land acquisition in Kannur despite similar procedures in Palakkad; claims projects worth over ₹40,000 crore have been completed through KIIFB; warns investigation could jeopardise proposed projects, including industrial park near Kannur airport

Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader M.V. Jayarajan has accused the Congress-led UDF government in Keralam of using a Vigilance investigation into land acquisition for Kerala Infrastructure Investment Board (KIIFB) projects to obstruct development, particularly in Kannur.

He alleged that the government order dated October 30, 2026, selectively targeted land acquisition in Kannur, despite similar procedures having been followed in Palakkad under the same central legislation.

Speaking to reporters in Kannur on Sunday, Mr. Jayarajan said the government was undermining development projects worth nearly ₹60,000 crore that had received administrative approval, been tendered or were under construction through KIIFB. He said projects worth more than ₹40,000 crore had already been completed, including roads, bridges, school buildings, hospitals and government offices.

The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau has been directed to conduct a detailed investigation into the procedures followed in acquiring 4,896 acres in Kannur at a cost of approximately ₹12,240 crore. The government order also refers to the acquisition of 470 acres in Palakkad, taking the total to 5,366 acres, with an estimated expenditure of ₹12,710 crore. However, Mr. Jayarajan questioned why the investigation was specifically directed at Kannur and why a special team had been constituted for the purpose.

He pointed out that Revenue Minister A.P. Anilkumar had informed the Assembly on October 29, in reply to a question, that the land in Kannur and Palakkad had been acquired under the central land acquisition law enacted in 2013. The land was acquired by special tahsildars for KIIFB and KINFRA projects.

According to the Minister’s reply, the compensation value was initially fixed through an order dated April 12, 2022. A subsequent order, however, provided for reductions of up to 80% from the basic value for land that had undergone physical changes, including areas previously subjected to quarrying.

Mr. Jayarajan said landowners had challenged the valuation in court. Following judicial directions, a committee appointed by the district administration examined the land, and the court accepted its report, he added.

“The Vigilance inquiry was politically motivated and intended to weaken KIIFB, which finances infrastructure projects because the State treasury lacks sufficient funds for large-scale development after meeting salary and pension commitments,” he said.

Mr. Jayarajan warned that the investigation could jeopardise several proposed projects in Kannur, including a 1,000-acre industrial park near Kannur International Airport, an education hub, and bridges and roads. He asked how the government intended to finance the remaining projects, noting that the Public Works Department alone had commitments of around ₹2,500 crore.

He demanded clarity on alternative funding arrangements and the future of projects already approved and awarded to contractors. He alleged that several Congress leaders had received compensation for acquired land. articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: Thousands turn up for INDIA bloc rally from across the country
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

Some travelled for nearly 48 hours in sleeper buses following the cancellation of train services. Others booked rail tickets from multiple stations to get around restrictions on bulk reservations. At least one walked in from a hospital ward. All negotiated multiple barriers on the way into Delhi, arriving from far-flung corners of the country in the thousands for the INDIA bloc rally on Sunday.
Chalo Dilli protests: Follow LIVE updates from the Opposition rally on November 1, 2026

The reasons that brought them to Delhi varied. For many, it was the only way to register their anger over being struck off electoral rolls. For some, it was a maiden visit to the capital. For others, it was a political pilgrimage that they hoped would bring long-anticipated change.

All of them converged on the muddy grounds of Ramlila Maidan, where white plastic chairs sank into the rain-soaked earth and shoes left deep imprints. Crowds spilled beyond the venue, with many still making their way towards the grounds even after the rally had ended.

“You can break one stick easily, but if you bundle 10 sticks together, they cannot be broken. Today’s protest symbolises that bundle of sticks,” said Tejender, an IT employee who had arrived with his wife from Gurugram.

He said he was attending the rally “for a better future for our children”. His list of grievances was long, ranging from the state of education and healthcare to what he described as “vote chori (theft)”, which, he felt, tied together many of the country’s problems.

Sheikh Abdul Rafiq, who travelled from Adilabad in Telangana, claimed that 15,000 people had come from the State despite what he described as efforts to restrict travel. The special trains were not allowed. Bulk bookings were blocked. In the end, he said, the group decided to spend their own money to book sleeper buses. For him, the journey was worth the effort because he felt political change was just around the corner.

If Mr. Rafiq spoke of change, another Telangana resident, Abdul Kaleem from Suryapet district, said he was there only to flag the “injustice”. Nearly 80% of the people in his village had lost their votes during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, he claimed. “I was born here; I studied here; I live here,” he said, but to get his name on the electoral rolls, he needed documents concerning his father and grandfather, which his family cannot find.

Zubair, a resident of Mominpura in central Nagpur, Maharashtra, echoed the sentiment. He has been running from pillar to post to get his family member’s names included in the electoral rolls, but it seems futile. Attending protests in the capital may, perhaps, deliver what all the running around back home failed to do, he hoped. “I was here for the October 10 protests too,” he said.
A scene from the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ march from Minto Bridge to Ramlila Maidan, in New Delhi, on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma

articles.title: KTR: KCR will come back to save farmers from Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

articles.title: Coal India’s production increases 19% as mining recovers after monsoon slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In a statement, the Coal India said, “The achievement assumes greater significance in view of the need to augment coal stocks at thermal power plants amid rising power demand.”

Coal India’s production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT)on a year-on-year basis in October, indicative of mining activity of the country’s largest producer picking up after being dampened because of monsoons.

The Kolkata-headquartered miner said that its supplies to the power sector also increased 19% to touch 57.1 MT. Overall supplies during the month surged 19% on a year-over-year basis to scale 70.3 MT. Both supplies to the power sector and overall supplies scaled record-highs in a single month, the company said.
About evacuation, it said that it loaded on an average 310 rakes per day — to the power sector — in October.

In a statement, the Coal India said, “The achievement assumes greater significance in view of the need to augment coal stocks at thermal power plants amid rising power demand, while disruptions caused by unseasonal rainfall, the Puja festivities and impact of a cyclone posed challenges to the operational performance.”

articles.title: Bhutan builds 108 stupas in 9 hours, dedicates No. 76 to PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk says gesture recognises India’s steadfast support for realisation of Gelephu Mindfulness City

Bhutan King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk on Sunday (November 1, 2026) dedicated one of the 108 Buddhist stupas erected in a nine-hour construction feat to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a mark of appreciation for India’s support for the country’s ambitious Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) project.
About 40,000 trained volunteers built the 108 Jangchub Chortens in what could be a potentially record-breaking royal initiative to lay the spiritual foundation of the planned city.
About 240 km south-southeast of Bhutan’s capital, Thimphu, Gelephu borders Assam’s Chirang district. King Wangchuk envisions the city as a spirituality-driven global economic hub.

The King, other members of the royal family, top officials and foreign dignitaries faced Chorten Number 79 from the ceremonial ground as thousands of people around chanted a six-syllable Tibetan Buddhist mantra a billion times while the volunteers completed the mission between 3 a.m. and 12 noon.

About two hours later, the focus shifted to Chorten Number 76, which the King dedicated to Mr. Modi “as an enduring symbol” of his “profound appreciation” for the latter’s “unwavering commitment and India’s steadfast support for the realisation” of GMC. Bhutanese officials said the number was chosen because Mr. Modi turned 76 more than a month ago.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, who represented India for ‘Project 108’, thanked the King for dedicating Chorten 76 to Mr. Modi. “This remarkable milestone is an enduring symbol of the deep spiritual and civilisational bonds between our two nations,” he said, congratulating Bhutan on the achievement.

Each 15 metres tall and 108 metres apart, the Jangchub Chortens, or Buddhist stupas, stand in a single meandering file along the Mau Chhu River, Gelephu’s lifeline. Built with steel and other improvised building materials, they mark a departure from the traditional use of stone and earth.

Addressing the people after the completion of Project 108, King Wangchuk said he had been worried that the construction of 108 stupas in a single day might not succeed. “People from every walk of life and every generation came together to make this possible,” he said, underscoring the Bhutanese collective spirit and ability to achieve “anything impossible”.

He said the same spirit would help Bhutan overcome natural calamities, economic crises, and other challenges. The King also expressed gratitude to Bhutan’s patrons, sponsors, supporters, and well-wishers. “Prime Minister Modi and the government of India have been enormously supportive of Bhutan and of the vision of Gelephu Mindfulness City,” he said.

articles.title: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers keep up protests
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The garment sector is the backbone of Bangladesh's export-driven economy, employing millions of workers and generating the bulk of the country's foreign earnings

Bangladesh formed a new board on Sunday (November 1, 2026) to review the minimum wage for garment workers, as authorities sought to quell protests that have disrupted key industrial hubs around Dhaka.
Despite the move, thousands of workers continued demonstrations in industrial areas around Dhaka on Sunday (November 1, 2026), leading to clashes with police who fired tear gas and sound grenades.
The garment sector is the backbone of Bangladesh's export-driven economy, employing millions of workers and generating the bulk of the country's foreign earnings.
The new wage board includes representatives of the government, workers, and factory owners.
"For the last three days, we have been discussing this issue with labour leaders and factory owners," Labour Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury said at a news conference in Dhaka.
"A coterie seeking to destabilise the government and cause public suffering has been exploiting our workers," he added, as he announced the new Board and urged workers to return to factories.
Labour leaders said their grievances extended beyond the creation of the Board, citing inflation and rising household expenses.
Workers currently earn about 13,000 taka ($106) a month, according to Kalpona Akhter of the Bangladesh Centre for Workers Solidarity.
"This time we are demanding a bit more than 30,000 taka, considering inflation and the rising cost of living," Mr. Akhter told AFP .
Thousands of factories across the country produce clothing including T-shirts, jeans, and sweaters for major retailers in Europe and the United States.

articles.title: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads in latest weapons drill
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded
North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported on Sunday (November 1, 2026), the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them.

The test, conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026), came after the nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system, and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded.
The North has denied responsibility and vowed to further fortify its border areas and resume its loudspeaker campaign.

Saturday's (October 31, 2026) test was conducted to "assess adaptation to combat and power of a cluster-bomb warhead to be tipped on tactical ballistic missiles", the official Korean Central News Agency reported on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Officials said it confirmed the weapon "is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 12 to 13 hectares with its highest-density power".

"Within this year we will enable units to select and use all those types according to operational aims and specific features of targets," said the general director of the North's Missile Administration.
Photos released by KCNA showed a projectile firing from a mobile launcher, with an orange exhaust plume. Another image showed multiple cluster-bomb impacts on an island target.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was not present on Saturday (October 31, 2026), although he had overseen a test-launch of cluster-bomb warheads mounted on a ballistic missile in April, accompanied by his daughter Ju Ae.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported on Sunday (November 1, 2026), the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was not present on Saturday (October 31, 2026), although he had overseen a test-launch of cluster-bomb warheads mounted on a ballistic missile in April, accompanied by his daughter Ju Ae.

articles.title: Historic win, humongous challenges
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme

At the end of the first round of Brazil’s presidential elections, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva looked like a leader on his way out after a record third term. He trailed Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2% to 47%, hurt by an abstention rate of 21%, the highest since 1998, as many of his supporters stayed home.

In the three weeks that followed, Mr. Lula managed a remarkable turnaround, helped by several factors. First, the day after the first round, thousands of students from the Fluminense Federal University marched through the streets of Niteroi to stand against Bolsonarism. Days later, thousands more young people occupied Candelaria Square in Rio de Janeiro. Similar student, youth and workers’ marches soon spread across urban Brazil. The protesters gathered without party banners, united less by support for Mr. Lula than by opposition to Bolsonarism, a far-right movement opposed to institutions, supportive of high-handed actions against crime and eager to curtail civil liberties. The newspaper O Globo described the marches as the Left’s return to the streets after more than a decade of absence.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Historic win, humongous challenges. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India in Space / space programme / space programme / ISRO

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.
